item.title: Early domination turns to shutout depression for Detroit Red Wings
item.description: DENVER – What an aggravating evening for the Detroit Red Wings. They did so many things right at the start, dominating their opponent on their ice, only for it all to go to waste amid a sea of penalties and punches. Their old rival, the Colorado Avalanche, scored twice during a penalty-filled second period on Saturday, Nov. 7, at Ball Arena, too much of a lead for the Wings to overcome against such a good opponent. The final score was 4-0, the Wings' third straight loss and fourth in five games. The outing highlighted the difference between the teams. The Avalanche's best – Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Martin Necas – feasted, combining for 10 points. Daniil Tarasov didn't stand a chance. YOUTH EFFECT: Gear in stall, place on plane: Young D-men earn respect from Red Wings The Wings' best couldn't find the net. As the score grew the tempers flared, and midway through the third period, two players neither side wanted to see fight –for the Wings, Moritz Seider; for the Avalanche, their captain, Gabriel Landeskog – brawled, exchancing multiple punches before officials intervened. The outing was part of a stretch pitting the Wings against some of the top teams in the NHL: The Florida Panthers (who they beat), Tampa Bay Lightning (a loss) and Vegas Golden Knights (also a loss). In both the Lightning and Avalanche games, the Wings struggled on draws, having lost their best faceoff expert when Dylan Larkin left the team Oct. 29 to wait out a trade. Who played Another healthy scratch for 2023 first-round pick Nate Danielson, with John Leonard subbing onto the third line instead, next to J.T. Compher and Michael Rasmussen. The other lines had Emmitt Finnie with Alex DeBrincat and Viktor Arvidsson, Andrew Copp with Michael Brandsegg-Nygard and Lucas Raymond, and Sheldon Dries with Carter Mazur and Keegan Kolesar. EURO SPIN: Henrik Zetterberg says Detroit Red Wings did Steve Yzerman dirty On the back end, Seider paired with Ben Chiarot, Justin Faulk with William Wallinder and Anton Johansson with Andreas Englund. Energetic start Brandsegg-Nygard tested Mackenzie Blackwood with a backhand attempt in the opening minute, part of a strong start for the Wings. By the midpoint of the first period, they had a 6-1 edge in shots. It great more lopsided when DeBrincat sprang Finnie for a breakaway, which ended with Blackwood turning away another backhand shot. With four minutes to go in the period, the Wings had a 10-1 edge in shots. After 20 minutes, it was 13-5.. Everything goes badly After a penalty-free first period, the second was nothing but ruts to the penalty boxes. Chiarot went off 51 seconds into the period. Four minutes later, it was Wallinder. While he was in the box, Seider and Nazem Kadri got into it behind Colorado's net, landing each a roughing call. Then Faulk was called for interference, at 7:59. While he served that penalty, Necas put the Avs up by a goal when T.J. Hughes' rebound landed right in front of Necas, who had a half-open net with Tarasov

item.title: Kentucky HC Will Stein gets 100% real on ‘no moral victories’ after loss to Tennessee
item.description: Randy Sartin-Imagn Images Kentucky HC Will Stein gets 100% real on ‘no moral victories’ after loss to Tennessee appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Kentucky football watched Tennessee fans troll the Wildcats following Saturday’s 34-6 trouncing. This loss surely alters both the SEC title game and College Football Playoff picture. But it also got UK coach Will Stein dropping 100% honesty after the game. Stein takes his biggest loss of his young head coaching career. Such a win would’ve increased UK’s chances of making a long-awaited trip to the conference championship. Plus impress the CFP committee in the process. But Stein dropped this eight-word admission after the defeat. “There really aren’t a lot of moral victories,” Stein told reporters after the game . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He also described how “uncharacteristic plays” did the Wildcats in during the drubbing. Will Stein’s opening statement following the loss at #16 Tennessee pic.twitter.com/BLaQJyfQuk — Cats Coverage (@Cats_Coverage) November 8, 2026 Kentucky now helps create quite the logjam in the SEC. So UK joins the Volunteers , Alabama and Texas at 7-2 teams all vying for a spot in Atlanta on Dec. 5 with the conference title on the line. Except now the Vols and the Crimson Tide own the tiebreaker edge over the Wildcats, by virtue of their victories over UK. So Stein and Kentucky must win out, then have lots of outside factors play into UK’s favor. Certainly one more loss by the aforementioned three 7-2 teams can boost Kentucky’s case. But the Wildcats face a daunting road. Kentucky hosts No. 24 Florida in Lexington next, with the loser potentially facing elimination from the SEC title game and CFP race. No. 18 Missouri then follows and surely, the Tigers will want to redeem themselves from their own letdown loss Saturday to Texas. Finally, Stein gets his taste of the Bluegrass State rivalry in facing Louisville to close out the season. Related: Georgia’s Kirby Smart reveals the most impressive aspect of win over Ole Miss Related: Alabama RB Daniel Hill brings out the belt after beating LSU in Death Valley

item.title: ‘We had a chance’: Lane Kiffin baffled after LSU loss to Alabama
item.description: Sep 19, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Louisiana State Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin looks on during the second quarter against the Mississippi Rebels at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images The No. 14 LSU Tigers moved the ball up and down the field against No. 5 Alabama on Saturday night, outgaining the Crimson Tide by 172 yards in Baton Rouge. But that didn’t matter much on the scoreboard, as LSU fell 31-13 for its third loss of the season. After the game, head coach Lane Kiffin admitted that he was struggling to make sense of it. Kiffin pointed to some impressive individual numbers from his offense and said he couldn’t believe they only added up to 13 points, calling the loss “really disappointing.” LSU’s Rough Night LSU entered the season with national title expectations in Kiffin’s first year in Baton Rouge, after he rebuilt the roster through the transfer portal. But the Tigers had already lost twice entering Saturday’s game against Alabama, including an emotional loss to Ole Miss , Kiffin’s former team, and an overtime loss at Kentucky. On Saturday, LSU went 0-for-4 on fourth down, the most attempts without a conversion in Kiffin’s career. The Tigers also made four trips to the red zone and came away with just one touchdown and one field goal. LSU briefly took the lead late in the third quarter, but Alabama answered with a 32-yard punt return by Ryan Coleman-Williams. On the next play, Keelon Russell hit Cederian Morgan for a 25-yard touchdown, and the Crimson Tide scored the final 21 points of the game. The loss dropped LSU to 6-3, and its chances of making the College Football Playoff fell from 51% to 25%, according to ESPN’s Allstate Playoff Predictor. ‘We had a chance’ After the game, Kiffin pointed out that his offense put up plenty of yards, but it didn’t translate to points. “I was looking at a sheet and it said Sam [Leavitt] had 380 yards passing and Jackson Harris had 11 [receptions] for 166 [yards] and Trey’Dez [Green] had 10 [receptions] for 85 [yards]. I wouldn’t think that would equal 13 points,” Kiffin said, via ESPN’s Alex Scarborough . “But you got to score touchdowns in the red zone.” When asked what’s keeping his team from making winning plays, Kiffin didn’t have much of an answer. “I don’t know,” he said. “We had a chance.” Kiffin also admitted that he didn’t expect LSU to be 6-3 at this point in the season, and things won’t get any easier next week, as LSU hosts Arch Manning and a Texas team coming off a controversial win over Missouri . “No, I did not think that, but it is where we are, and we can’t change that. So, we got to go back to work. Don’t have time to sit around and feel bad. Got a top-10 team coming in here in Texas,” Kiffin said. “It’s one thing, probably the one good thing about playing these types of teams in a row like this, ‘Hey, you got a chance to play another national game and get back on track,'” he added. item.title: Tennessee Ends Kentucky’s Winning Streak
item.description: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Tony Siracusa, CFB Managing Editor The Kentucky football team has been one of the darlings of the 2026 college football season. Coming off their bye week, Will Stein’s club entered Saturday riding a six-game winning streak. In addition, they sat sixth in the first college football playoff rankings. That’s the highest they’ve ever been. However, they faced a daunting task heading to a place where they’ve had little to no success. Unfortunately for the BBN, about everything that could go wrong did. As a result, the Cats dropped from a first-place tie. It wasn’t pretty, but let’s break it down as Tennessee ends Kentucky’s winning streak 34-6. Tennessee Ends Kentucky’s Winning Streak Had Their Chances After punting on their first drive, the Kentucky offense had a good chance at getting on the board. However, on a third and eight from the Tennessee 39, Kenny Minchey was picked off in the end zone, ending UK’s scoring chances. It was the UK signal caller’s first interception since the Alabama game in week two. The Kentucky defense held once again, and for most of the first quarter neither team got anything going on offense. That was until the end of the period. Daune Morris found a seam against a Kentucky blitz and was off to the races, 66 yards for a touchdown. From there, both teams traded field goals and it was 10-3 Volunteers. Kentucky’s second turnover of the half, a fumble by CJ Baxter, gave the Vols good field position. However, the Kentucky defense held again, allowing no points. Right before the intermission, the Wildcats had their best drive of the game. Starting at their own four-yard line, Minchey marched the Cats down to the Tennessee seven. A third down throw to all-SEC tight end Willie Rodriguez fell incomplete. Unfortunately for the BBN, they got a no-call of what looked like pass interference, which forced another field goal, making it 10-6 at the half. How is this not pass interference? pic.twitter.com/z8COREhPSR — Tristan Pharis (@TristanUda) November 8, 2026 Considering how poorly Kentucky had played, you had to feel good about the second half. However, you would be wrong as Tennessee ended Kentucky’s winning streak 34-6. Rocky Flop In each of Kentucky’s three straight SEC road wins, they trailed in the second half. There was no reason to think it couldn’t happen again. But playing in Neyland Stadium has always been rough for Kentucky, and this was no different. UT got a field goal to start the half, and then the Cats fell off the cliff. A Minchey fumble led to a touchdown pass from backup quarterback Faizon Brandon to Mike Matthews, and just like that it was 20-6. On the next series, Minchey was sacked on a fourth and one at midfield. Tennessee took advantage again as Desean Bishop took it in from five yards out, and the lead was 21. item.title: Big Ten standings: What Oregon's win over Ohio State means for College Football Playoff
item.description: Big Ten standings: What Oregon's win over Ohio State means for College Football Playoff originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The two preseason favorites in the Big Ten finally went head-to-head in Week 10. Neither of them will leave the game in a position to make the conference title game. Oregon took down No. 11 Ohio State, 41-28, as Dylan Raiola threw a pair of touchdown passes, while the Buckeyes' offense struggled to keep up behind Luke Fahey. In a season where UCLA has unexpectedly emerged to become the conference leader, there's been another shake-up in the Big Ten playoff race. Here's a look at how the Ducks' win will impact the final stretch at the top of the Big Ten. MORE: Is Ohio State out of CFP race with loss to Oregon? Oregon takes down Ohio State When Bo Jackson scored his second touchdown of the game around the end of the first quarter, it appeared Ohio State could overcome Julian Sayin's absence to beat an unranked Ducks team fighting to even keep its playoff hopes alive. But a 17-point second quarter — including a gutsy call from Dan Lanning to go for a touchdown instead of a field goal before halftime — changed the game. Oregon ripped off 31 points in the middle quarters to Ohio State's none, and that was easily enough to prevent Fahey (360 yards, 2 TDs) from making a comeback. The Buckeyes quarterback threw an interception that led to a touchdown and had a fairly modest connection with star receiver Jeremiah Smith (76 yards, TD). With the win in Columbus, Oregon improved to 6-3 overall and 4-2 in Big Ten play, while Ohio State dropped its second-straight game, also falling to 6-3 and 4-2 in Big Ten play. OREGON IS DOMINATING OHIO STATE😳 (via CBS) https://t.co/Df72csZOtK — On3 (@On3) November 7, 2026 MORE: Breaking down Oregon's path to CFP after upset win over Buckeyes Big Ten playoff contenders Team Overall Conference Week 11 UCLA 9-0 6-0 vs. Illinois Indiana 8-1 5-1 vs. USC Oregon 6-3 4-2 vs. Michigan Ohio State 6-3 4-2 vs. Northwestern Iowa 7-2 4-2 vs. Purdue USC 7-2 4-2 at Indiana Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images No. 5 UCLA (9-0, 6-0) Unexpectedly, UCLA is the clear-cut favorite in the Big Ten in Year 1 under Bob Chesney. The Bruins remained unbeaten in Week 10 by taking down Minnesota, and they have favorable matchups against Illinois and Michigan over the next two weeks. A West Coast matchup against USC in the last week of the regular season will be the big test for the Bruins, potentially even deciding their playoff fate. No. 6 Indiana (8-1, 5-1) Curt Cignetti's squad remains in a good spot, even with Week 10 off. The key matchup remaining is against USC in Week 11, a game that will likely decide whether or not the Hoosiers will be playing in the Big Ten Championship. A loss could also put Indiana at risk of the committee snubbing them from the field altogether, lacking any key resume wins this year. Oregon (6-3, 4-2) The Ducks aren't dead yet. It won't be

item.title: Louisville Defeats Georgia Tech, 44-17
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - NOVEMBER 7: Tre Richardson #0 of the Louisville Cardinals runs with the ball before scoring a touchdown against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets during the second quarter at Bobby Dodd Stadium on November 7, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Colin Hubbard/Getty Images) | Getty Images What a lovely evening. Despite the odd start with special teams blunders, I think most would agree this was the most complete performance of the season thus far. This team has had similar blow out wins against FSU and Stanford, but in those games it took a minute for the team to hit the gas a turn away. But in this one it never felt like Georgia Tech was in the game. After scoring on the first drive, the defense had to force multiple 3-and-outs to start their game before they finally conceded 3 points thanks to the special teams. Brohm looked as equally as frustrated as the rest of us, but it didn’t last long as the offense looked unstoppable and the defense looked….good? The game in its entirety was as close to perfect as fans have been hoping for all season, and for it to come in November when there’s still 3 very important games ahead could not be better timing. Lincoln looked in control all game as he finished 17/25 for 182 yds and 2 TDs, to go along with his 81 yards on the ground. Treyshun Hurry did a fantastic job filling in for the injured McCoy as he reeled in 8 receptions for 104 yards and a TD. The Brown Bros. rushed for a modest combined total of 92 yards on just 16 carries against one of, if not the worst rushing defenses in the conference. But it didn’t matter as the offense got pretty much whatever they wanted. And I’d be remiss if I didn’t mention this gorgeous jet sweep to Tre Richardson for a 52-yard TD, his second of the night. TRE RICHARDSON. AGAIN. 🤯 📺 @accnetwork x @LouisvilleFB pic.twitter.com/Ntf6DFlkql — ACC Football (@ACCFootball) November 8, 2026 Meanwhile on the defense they made life hell for whoever was playing QB tonight. Tech couldn’t seem to figure out what would work between Mendoza and Adamson, and it wasn’t much of anything between the two. The defense held Ga. Tech to an outstanding 4 of 17 on 3rd down, and 5.4 yards per pass and just 3.4 yards per rush. But the biggest numbers of the night came from the defensive front as they had 4 sacks, 7 TFLs, and 5 batted balls. It seemed like even when the commitee of QBs got time to throw, there was either pressure coming and/or hands blocking throwing lanes. It was a fantastic effort from the defense and one that I think we all hope the team can build on as they entire the final quarter of the season with a lot left on the table. It’s not often you get to kick your feet up and watch your team trounce a conference foe while other certain teams are getting blown out. So enjoy nights like tonight. We’ve all earned this one.

item.title: IND 2-0 up vs NZ in ODI series: List of teams who have lost a ODI series after taking 2-0 lead
item.description: IND 2-0 up vs NZ in ODI series: List of teams who have lost a ODI series after taking 2-0 lead originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: India lead New Zealand 2-0 after two close wins, and history now offers a warning. Only a handful of teams have thrown away such a lead in a series of five or more matches. India themselves have suffered this fate once before, and the details may surprise fans. Can New Zealand come back from 0-2 down? Full record of bilateral ODI comebacks in history India head into the third ODI against New Zealand with a 2-0 lead, though cricket history shows that such an advantage is not always the safe position it appears to be. A small group of teams have let a similar lead slip in a bilateral series, and the names on that list include India themselves. The hosts were beaten in Auckland by five wickets, a result reached under the DLS method, and then lost again in Wellington by four runs, once more through DLS. Those two results have put India in front in the five-match series, and the remaining games will decide whether New Zealand can mount a recovery. The record books say it has been done only rarely, as a 0-2 deficit has been overturned just five times in ODI series of five or more matches. The sections below set out who has managed it, how India fell short in the past, and when the rest of the current series will be played. MORE: Rahul hailed as India clinch a narrow win in Wellington Teams who lost an ODI series after leading 2-0: Full list South Africa have achieved this twice, while Bangladesh, Pakistan and Australia have each done it once. That makes it a very uncommon feat, since it has happened only five times in more than 50 years of men’s ODI cricket. The table below lists the sides that surrendered a 2-0 lead, along with the team that came back. Team that lost after leading 2-0 Team that won from 0-2 down Matches in series Season Pakistan South Africa 5 2003-04 Zimbabwe Bangladesh 5 2004-05 India Pakistan 6 2004-05 England South Africa 5 2015-16 India Australia 5 2018-19 How South Africa, Bangladesh and Australia pulled off famous ODI comebacks In 2003, Pakistan took a 2-0 lead at home with wins in Lahore, by 8 runs and then by 42 runs. South Africa answered by winning in Faisalabad by 13 runs and then twice in Rawalpindi, by six wickets and by seven wickets, to take the series 3-2. Two years later, Zimbabwe won the first two games in Dhaka, by 102 runs and 31 runs. Habibul Bashar’s Bangladesh then took the last three, in Dhaka by 40 runs and in Chattogram by 58 runs and eight wickets respectively, to complete a historic turnaround. In 2016, England went 2-0 up in South Africa after winning in Bloemfontein by 39 runs via DLS, and in Port Elizabeth, by five wickets. AB de Villiers’ side then won at Centurion by seven wickets, in Johannesburg by one wicket and in Cape Town by five wickets. MORE: Rahul vs Axar at No. 5: Why India should prefer R

item.title: Angels rumors: Infielder joins Zach Neto as potential offseason trade candidate
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Angels rumors: Infielder joins Zach Neto as potential offseason trade candidate appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Zach Neto has already been floated as a potential trade chip for the Los Angeles Angels this offseason, and now another young infielder is being mentioned alongside him. With the franchise at a crossroads, first baseman Nolan Schanuel could also be on the move if the club decides to rebuild. MLB.com’s Rhett Bollinger noted that both players are firmly entrenched in the Angels’ infield, but their futures could depend on which direction the team takes. “The Angels have Zach Neto entrenched at shortstop and Nolan Schanuel at first base, but either could be a trade candidate if they decide to rebuild,” Bollinger wrote. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Angels are coming off a brutal 2026 season in which they lost 100 games. On top of that, the organization is in the middle of a major transition. Arte Moreno agreed to sell the team to Kroenke Sports & Entertainment for a reported $4 billion, and the Angels are not expected to hire a new general manager or manager until the sale is approved. Interim GM John Mozeliak is set to depart when his contract expires in December. Neto has been at the center of trade speculation for months. The Boston Red Sox reportedly had strong interest in the 25-year-old shortstop ahead of the trade deadline, and MLB Network’s Jon Morosi recently suggested the Angels should explore the market . “This is the time to gauge interest in Zach Neto and Reid Detmers,” Morosi said on MLB Network’s “Hot Stove.” “It’s not about winning a World Series in 2027.” It is easy to see why teams would be interested. Neto slugged 27 home runs and drove in 77 runs in 157 games in 2026, and he has three years of team control remaining. Schanuel, meanwhile, is 24 years old and coming off a solid campaign in which he hit .276 with seven home runs, 49 RBIs and a .736 OPS in 107 games. The former first-round pick has been a steady presence at first base since debuting just weeks after being drafted in 2023. For now, any major moves will likely have to wait until the ownership change is finalized. But if the new regime chooses to tear things down, Neto and Schanuel could be two of the most intriguing names on the trade market. Related: Angels rumors: Potential Zach Neto trade update will catch shortstop-needing teams’ attention Related: Ex-Angels GM joins Braves for 2027 season

item.title: Everett outlasts Conemaugh Township in District 5-2A championship
item.description: RICHLAND TOWNSHIP — Conemaugh Township eyed its second upset of the week when it took on to top-seeded Everett in the District 5 Class 2A volleyball championship, Saturday, Nov. 7, at Pitt-Johnstown. Like its semifinal final contest against Windber, the title tilt went the distance. Unfortunately, Conemaugh Township could not complete the rally, as the Warriors earned a 23-25, 25-23, 25-19, 11-25, 15-12 victory. "You can't wait until the third and fourth game to put the pedal to the metal," said Conemaugh Township coach Laura Swank. "The nerves got to some of my players. Once we settled in, we had a battle. Everett, they're a phenomenal team. They're very scrappy. They don't give up." Champs again Berlin Brothersvalley bests Meyersdale for 4th straight D5-1A title Ones to watch Berlin bids for 4th straight D5 volleyball title, Class 2A wide open There were nine ties in the first set. After an 8-1 run by the Warriors, Conemaugh Township went on a 7-0 surge for a 22-21 advantage. Conemaugh Township closed the set, tallying 3 of the final 4 points, taking a 1-0 lead in the match. The second set was another battle. Trailing 17-12, Conemaugh Township notched five straight points to even things. There were three more ties from that point, but Everett came up with some big kills to close the set and tie the match at a set apiece. It was a trio of Everett runs that led to a triumph in the third set. Trailing 7-2, the Warriors tallied four straight and were down by only a point. Down 10-8, Everett notched five in a row for its first lead in the set. The Warriors put the set out of reach with an 8-1 run in the latter stages of the set. With its season hanging in the balance, Conemaugh Township dominated the fourth set. It never trailed once, forcing a fifth and deciding set. However, Everett responded in the fifth set. The defending champs did not trail. Tied at 10 apiece, the Warriors rattled off the next three points and recorded back-to-back kills to claim the championship. Conemaugh Township was led by junior Sarah Swank's 34 kills and 17 digs, while senior Danika Black provided nine blocks, nine digs and seven kills. Fellow senior Averie Seibert dished out 34 assists to go along with nine digs, while Mary Matera added 23 assists and 11 digs. Quinn Moser and Mya Nemeth combined for 36 digs, and sophomore Cora Oswalt delivered 14 blocks and 11 kills. "I'm very proud of them," Coach Swank said. "We have heart and they will battle to the end. Nobody quit. They put their best effort forward and gave it their all." Somerset sweeps Central Mountain for Class 4A championship Somerset avenged a regular season loss to Central Mountain with a 25-20, 25-14, 25-17 victory in the District 5-6-8 Class 4A championship game at Mount Aloysius College. Kaycee Stairs recorded 17 kills and three blocks, while Thressa Ledney tallied eight kills, six aces and six digs for the Golden Eagles. item.title: Miami’s game-tying touchdown denied by refs in controversial call during loss to Notre Dame
item.description: No. 1 Miami vs. No. 11 Notre Dame might have been the college football game of the year in South Bend on Saturday night. The Fighting Irish entered needing a signature win to get back in the good graces of the College Football Playoff Committee , and also seeking revenge for a season-opening loss to Miami last year that kept ND out of the playoff. Notre Dame took control early with a 24-7 lead, but the Hurricanes would mount a comeback. Heisman Trophy candidate Darian Mensah put Miami in position to tie the game late in the fourth quarter, but a controversial call kept the Hurricanes out of the end zone and ultimately sealed their fate. Notre Dame beat Miami, 31-24, to bolster its resume ahead of the playoff. It appeared Miami had briefly tied the game with under four minutes remaining when Mensah found tight end Elija Lofton in the corner of the end zone on fourth down, but the refs ruled that he didn’t complete the catch, which gave Notre Dame the ball on a turnover on downs. Loften caught the ball, and got both feet in-bounds, but the refs ruled that he did not perform an “act common to the game,” which essentially means he didn’t complete the catch before the Notre Dame defender knocked the ball away. Watch the play here. Elijah Lofton couldnt hold it Notre Dame big 4th down stop pic.twitter.com/hXiEXZgvVS — wok (@wokdior) November 8, 2026 Here’s another angle. TD OR NO?!?!?!! pic.twitter.com/gOEHWVUDDd — Grant Reacts (@GrantReacts1) November 8, 2026 In college football, a catch requires firm control, a body part down in bounds, and control long enough to perform an act common to the game. Lofton clearly had control. Was the play already over when Notre Dame defensive back Luke Talich stripped it? The play was reviewed the refs affirmed their initial call of no catch. Notre Dame went on to win. Miami suffered its first loss of the season. Do you think the refs got it right? That looks like a catch to me. Lofton stepped out of bounds and then the ball was knocked loss. Shouldn’t that step count as a common act? Let us know what you think in the comments.

item.title: Instant Recap: Michigan State Spartans Takes Down Michigan, 15-6
item.description: Nov 7, 2026; Ann Arbor, Michigan, USA; Michigan State Spartans wide receiver Chrishon McCray (13) runs the ball against the Michigan Wolverines at Michigan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect From early on in this game, and as many people already knew, it was clear that this was a game between two not good teams. Unfortunately for us Spartan fans, we have had a couple unlucky breaks while tonight’s opponent has had some good fortune in their season. Watching the two teams in the first half, one would imagine their records were closer than the reality. Michigan State got the ball first and moved the chains one time before punting. On their first defensive stand, Michigan State got a turnover when safety Devin Vaught came down with a pick after a pass went off an um receiver’s finger tips. Starting a yard inside um territory, the Spartans reached 4th & 2 on the first series. Coach Fitzgerald decided to be aggressive, and the play call was for a deep shot. Personally, I would have rather punted here to try pinning an unimpressive offense deep. Predictably, the deep shot did not pay off. Receiver Bryson Williams had a chance at it but dropped the pass. The two teams traded punts on their next possessions, totaling 17 yards of offense between them. On um’s ensuing drive, they had their best drive of the half, moving 71 yards in 13 plays over six and a half minutes. They reached the MSU 7, but a 3rd & 1 run lost a yard and brought out the field goal unit. The kick went off the near side upright and bounced out, keeping the game with no points on the board. Again, the two teams traded punts. Getting the ball right at the 50, the Spartans marched all the way to the 3-yard line before having to settle for a field goal, which Liam Boyd made. Just like that, the Spartans were ahead. MSU then forced a 3-and-out. Chrishon McCray muffed the punt reception but retrieved the fumble, and MSU took over at their own 44. MSU picked up a couple first downs, the second on a 35-yard pass to McCray that got the Spartans down to the 13. A bogus offensive pass interference penalty in the endzone pushed MSU back near the 20 and eventually led to another FG try, which Boyd comfortably made. There was only time for a kneel-down after the kickoff, and MSU took a 6-0 lead to the break. Our defense only gave up 78 total yards through two quarters. MSU started the second half on defense, and after giving up a first down on the first play, forced a punt. Unfortunately for us, that punt was allowed to land and it flatlined at the 1-yard line, pinning Alessio Milivojevic and the MSU offense against the goalline. Starting from the 1-yard line, Michigan State had, perhaps, their most impressive drive since week 2. The Spartans held the ball for 10:41 of game clock, ran 17 plays, and picked up 6 first downs. There were passes, runs, wildcats, and overall dominance from MSU. After reaching the um 12, the offense finally came to a ha

item.title: 1 thing I loved, 2 things I hated: Michigan Football vs MSU
item.description: ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 07: Savion Hiter #5 of the Michigan Wolverines is tackled by Cam Stodghill #12 of the Michigan State Spartans during a first half run at Michigan Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Michigan Wolverines lost to Michigan State for the first time since 2021, this time by a final score of 15-6. The Spartans largely owned the game from start to finish, as the final score is not as close as it may appear. Here is one thing I loved and two things I hated from tonight’s game. 1 thing I hated: Every single thing on offense It took the Wolverines a little while to get things going offensively, as the first possession resulted in a Tommy Carr interception while the second possession was a three-and-out. But things clicked on Michigan’s third drive of the game, and it was thanks to the power run game. Running back Bryson Kuzdzal took a handoff five yards up the middle on the first play of the drive. After a pass by Carr to Kuzdzal for a first down, Kuzdzal picked up 16 yards up the middle to pick up another first down. Kudzdal then a nine-yard run to pick up another first down for the Wolverines. It’s a shame the drive ended in a missed field goal, but the Wolverines picked up 71 yards on the drive, with 49 of them being on the ground. It was a solid drive that should have resulted in points, but it was a small glimmer of light in an otherwise supermassive black hole. But other that that drive, I can’t say anything else positively about Michigan’s offense. It was flat, uninspired and unsuccessful for a majority of the game. The Wolverines compiled a total of 64 yards on their other eight drives. All in all, Michigan threw for 138 yards and ran for 54 yards; Carr threw two interceptions and Kuzdzal lost a fumble. They only scored when the game was already over, and then proceeded to miss the two-point try. The offense should feel ashamed of this performance. To be shut out against one of the worst defenses in the country at home is absolutely embarrassing. Another thing I hated: Long drives on defense We’ve been very complimentary of Jay Hill and the defensive unit this season, but cracks in the armor started to show last weekend against Rutgers. Things weren’t all that great against the Spartans on Saturday night either. Michigan’s defense was on the field a lot on Saturday. The defense gave up drives consisting of six (three times), nine, 10 (twice) and 17 plays. The Spartans owned time of possession, taking up 38:07 of game clock. They wore out the Michigan defense early and often, running 75 total plays. MSU wide receiver Chrishon McCray led the way with six receptions for 92 yards. Bryson Williams also had one explosive reception for 36 yards, while Brandon Tullis led them on the ground with 25 carries for 86 yards. The offense certainly didn’t do the defense any favors tonight, but to give up nearly 300 total yards of offense to that team is unaccep

item.title: Bainbridge's Dodge claims Class 2A boys cross country championship
item.description: Last year, Bainbridge cross country standout Ryan Dodge helped the Spartans win the Class 2A team championship at Sun Willows Golf Course in Pasco. As a senior, Dodge felt what it was like to reach the top of the podium as an individual. Dodge crossed the finish line in 15 minutes, 27.8 second to easily win the 2A boys race Saturday, Nov. 7. Dodge led the field at the 1-mile and 2-mile splits and wasn't challenged down the stretch. North Central senior Elliot Yegge took second in 15:44, while Kingston senior Timothy Clark-Johnston finished fourth in 15:47.4. Bainbridge took seventh as a team, one spot ahead of Kingston. Olympic finished 12th. In what proved to be a much faster 3A boys race, 2025 champion Mana Voss of Central Kitsap placed fifth in 15:25.2. Hermiston (Ore.) junior Leroy Lozano Mejia placed first in 14:45.9 and Shorewood senior Elijah Graves placed second in 14:55.9. Gig Harbor High was the boys team state champion. In the 2A girls competition, Kingston senior Emma Grice ran 19:05.5 to place eighth, two spots ahead of Bainbridge senior Evelyn Shutske (19:10.1). Bainbridge junior Vega Hendrickson took 15th and Olympic senior Brynn Fulton placed 19th. As a team, Bainbridge finished sixth. In the 1B boys race, Crosspoint Christian junior Haowu Liu placed 19th. This article originally appeared on Kitsap Sun: Bainbridge's Dodge claims Class 2A boys cross country championship

item.title: LAFC caps off regular season with loss to Seattle Sounders
item.description: The MLS regular season officially came to an end as Saturday marked Decision Day, with LAFC falling 2-1 to Seattle Sounders FC at Lumen Field. The Black & Gold completed their 2026 campaign 12-11-11, finishing as the No. 6 seed in the Western Conference and earning a first-round matchup with St. Louis City SC. Under interim head coach Xavi Tamarit, the club went 1-2-3 to finish the year, with Saturday's defeat marking the end of a two-game win streak against Seattle. Los Angeles is now 15-8-4 all-time against the Seattle and just 2-5-3 on the road. LAFC quickly allowed the Sounders to grab momentum in the match after some poor goalkeeping by Cabral Carter in the opening minute. His pass towards Ryan Porteus and Mathieu Choinière was intercepted by Cristian Roldan, who quickly fed Albert Rusnák across the middle for an easy score. OFF TO A FLYING START ON DECISION DAY 🙂‍↕️ pic.twitter.com/vwl8eozljp — Seattle Sounders FC (@SoundersFC) November 8, 2026 Thirty minutes later, the Sounders doubled their lead. This time around, it was a close-range shot from Sebastian Gomez that deflected off LA's Eddie Segura and over the head of a helpless Carter to make it 2-0. Usual starting goalkeeper Hugo Lloris was held out of action with a back injury. It marked the third consecutive game that LAFC had fallen down 2-0 to open a match. Once again, the momentum quickly slipped out of their favor and left an uphill battle ahead. Despite a plethora of shot attempts and possession, the same issues continued to persist. A lack of cohesion, direction and intent left the Black & Gold looking uninspired as they fought to claw their way back into the match. Additionally, Sounders' goalkeeper Andrew Thomas made seven saves, his second-most in a single performance this year. It was not until the 82nd minute that Segura managed to get LA on the board, cashing in off a well-executed set-piece play. Leo Walta's free kick was first met by the head of Ryan Porteous, who picked up the assist as Segura came flying in to deliver a goal-scoring header of his own. Segura with the header 😤 pic.twitter.com/81kDvmkHt4 — LAFC (@LAFC) November 8, 2026 It was the first goal of the season for the defender, who hadn't found the back of the net since June 2025. There would be no equalizer for LA as Seattle picked up the three crucial points it needed to sneak into the postseason as the eighth seed. Their 46 points were just one behind LAFC's 47. Forward Jacob Shaffelburg entered Saturday's defeat in the 72nd minute as a substitute for Armindo Sieb and exited just eight minutes later after taking a hard hit along the sideline. Tamarit said after the match that Shaffelburg was taken to the hospital, speculating that he might have sustained broken ribs. Meanwhile, forward Denis Bouanga finished his season with 18 goals, falling just two short of becoming the first player in league history to score 20 or more in four consecutive seasons. He finished tied for sixth in goals, scoring the third-mos

item.title: St. Cloud State surrenders five points to Omaha as McLaughlin carted off ice
item.description: ST. CLOUD —The St. Cloud State men's hockey team faltered on the road against Omaha, going 0-1-1 this weekend to fall to 3-5-1 overall. In the first game, the Huskies battled back from a one-goal deficit to earn a 2-2 tie against the Mavericks on Friday night at Baxter Arena, but Omaha claimed the NCHC standings points with a 1-0 victory in a shootout following a scoreless overtime period. The Huskies struck early on the power play when freshman defenseman Will Sharpe scored his first collegiate goal just 1:49 into the contest. Omaha swiftly answered on a goal from Gavin Hodnett before Ryan McCleary paced the Mavs ahead in the second period. St. Cloud State responded in the third period after generating sustained pressure and capitalizing on another power-play opportunity. Following a 5-on-3 advantage, freshman forward Hayden Paupanekis generated a scoring opportunity, leading to sophomore defenseman Finn McLaughlin burying the tying goal into an open net. The Huskies looked much more polished in the final period, outshooting Omaha 17-6, but could not find the go-ahead goal. More: Charlie Lurie brings 'the best shot' you'll see to St. Cloud State hockey More: How William Ahlrik's pride for faceoffs has boosted St. Cloud State hockey More: Freshman Nolan Stevenson making early statement with St. Cloud State hockey McLaughlin added an assist for his first career multi-point game while goaltender Yan Shostak continued his strong play in net with 31 saves, highlighted by 17 in the second period, as the Huskies outshot Omaha 44-33 and converted 2-of-3 power-play chances. In the second game of the road trip, the Huskies continued their power play barrage with three additional PP scores from William Ahlrik, Nolan Roed and Carson Pilgrim, but could not keep up with the Mavs in a 5-3 loss, surrendering five points total for the weekend. St. Cloud State showed plenty of fight, erasing a two-goal deficit to pull even with Omaha in the third period, but a go-ahead score from Maxime Pellerin on the power play with 3:53 remaining and an empty-netter late handed the Huskies a hard-to-swallow loss. Shostak had 19 saves in the loss. To make matters worse for the Huskies, in the midst of the best weekend of his collegiate career, McLaughlin was carted off the ice behind the net after a heavy collision. SCSU Athletics does not have an update on McLaughlin's status at this time. SCSU player taken off the ice. Looks like McLaughlin. https://t.co/ePx32Dnu7h — Mavpuck (@Mavpuck) November 8, 2026 More: St. Cloud State's Jack Reimann exits game in loss vs. Arizona State McLaughlin transferred in from Minnesota, where he played in 31 games as a true freshman. The Canmore, Alberta, native has recorded two goals and three assists this season to pair with 10 blocks. The Huskies host No. 8 Minnesota Duluth next weekend in what is bound to be another competitive, but difficult weekend for a St. Cloud squad in the midst of gathering its footing in the early part of the season.

item.title: Steve Sarkisian made a bold declaration after No. 7 Texas beat No. 18 Missouri
item.description: COLUMBIA, MO - NOVEMBER 07: Steve Sarkisian of the Texas Longhorns celebrates after a win in an SEC football game between the Texas Longhorns and Missouri Tigers on Nov 7, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Columbia, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Head coach Steve Sarkisian and the No. 7 Texas Longhorns don’t pay any attention to the outside noise. Except when they do. “Missouri is winning this ballgame… better QB, better WR core, better RB, they’re more physical,” SEC Network studio analyst Peter Burns said Friday. “I’m really proud of our football team overall because our guys, they’re not naive to noise. As much as I would love to say, tune it all out — and we try our best to do that — I could hear the talk getting on the plane yesterday. I could hear the talk when we got here,” Sarkisian said. “Nobody believed we’d win the game. Nobody thought we were going to come here and win the game. Nobody thought we were we were tough enough at the line of scrimmage. Everyone thought we’d be pushed around.” Oddsmakers certainly thought more highly of Texas — the Longhorns were 2.5-point favorites over the Tigers on FanDuel . Nonetheless… With the 34-20 win over No. 18 Missouri, Sarkisian’s team is now 4-1 against top-25 opponents on the road and has four wins over ranked teams this season, the most in the country. “The DNA of this organization is mental and physical toughness, and I think that poured out of our pores today in this ball game today, and so I’m very proud of them for that. I’m very proud of the way they hung together, the way they responded to adversity,” Sarkisian said. “There is a toughness in our organization that is undeniable. Right when people want to count us out, we refuse to go away.”

item.title: How Patriots legend Rob Gronkowski truly felt about Tom Brady’s presence at his New England Hall of Fame ceremony
item.description: © Allen Eyestone via Imagn Content Services, LLC How Patriots legend Rob Gronkowski truly felt about Tom Brady’s presence at his New England Hall of Fame ceremony appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Rob Gronkowski had plenty of familiar faces in his corner for his New England Patriots Hall of Fame induction on Saturday, but one presence clearly stood out above the rest. The former tight end opened up about what it meant to have Tom Brady by his side for the big day. “It meant everything… He wanted to be here. It just meant a lot, man. Tom can be anywhere else. He’s the greatest player of all time. It just meant a lot to myself, my family, and to the fans, I’m sure as well,” Gronkowski said, via Justin Turpin . Rob Gronkowski on having Tom Brady at his Patriots Hall of Fame induction: “It meant everything… He wanted to be here. It just meant a lot, man. Tom can be anywhere else. He’s the greatest player of all time. It just meant a lot to myself, my family, and to the fans, I’m sure… pic.twitter.com/JF8oYLQLTv — Justin Turpin (@JustinmTurpin) November 7, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brady received a loud ovation from the crowd at Patriot Place Plaza, where many of Gronkowski’s former teammates and coaches gathered for the ceremony. The legendary quarterback also showed his former tight end some love on social media , reposting a video of the two embracing with a simple message. “That’s my 🐐,” Brady wrote. The mutual admiration makes sense. Brady and Gronkowski formed one of the most dominant quarterback-tight end duos in NFL history, winning three Super Bowls together in New England before reuniting with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to capture a fourth title in the 2020 season. Gronkowski was voted into the Patriots Hall of Fame by fans in April, in his first year of eligibility. He joined Brady, who was inducted in 2024. The honor caps a remarkable career in New England . Gronkowski spent nine seasons with the Patriots after being selected in the second round of the 2010 NFL Draft out of Arizona. He racked up 521 receptions for 7,861 yards and 79 touchdowns in the regular season, and his 80 total touchdowns rank first in franchise history. He was also a five-time Pro Bowler and four-time First-Team All-Pro. Patriots owner Robert Kraft was unable to attend the ceremony while recovering from back surgery, but he had high praise for Gronkowski when the honor was announced. “Rob became a fan favorite almost immediately and remained the standard at tight end for nearly a decade,” Kraft said. The celebration continues on Sunday, when Gronkowski will be honored at halftime of the Patriots’ game against the Green Bay Packers. Brady will be on hand for that one as well, calling the game from the FOX broadcast booth. item.title: Miami’s Darian Mensah connects with Cooper Barkate for 2nd half TD vs. Notre Dame
item.description: Stan Szeto-Imagn Images Miami’s Darian Mensah connects with Cooper Barkate for 2nd half TD vs. Notre Dame appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With Malachi Toney out for Miami football , Cooper Barkate is stepping up against Notre Dame. Barkate and Darian Mensah connected for a crucial touchdown to cut Notre Dame’s lead to 24-17 in the third quarter. The Hurricanes are STORMING back. Darian Mensah finds Cooper Barkate for his second TD of the second half to put Miami within a score of Notre Dame. pic.twitter.com/dw3rmB6DKu Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Underdog CFB (@UnderdogCFB) November 8, 2026 Mensah threw a great ball to the end zone, where Barkate was able to adjust his body and make the spectacular catch for the touchdown. Miami was held without a touchdown in the first half as the Fighting Irish went into halftime with a 17-3 lead. Mensah was stuffed as he tried to run for a touchdown at the goal-line . CJ Carr had gotten the better of his high-profile matchup with Mensah with two first-half touchdowns, including a beautiful throw to Jordan Faison. He then extended the Fighting Irish’s lead to 24-3 when he found Micah Gilbert in the end zone in their first drive of the second half. But Mensah and No. 1 Miami have stormed back with two touchdown passes in a row. First he found Elija Lofton to cap off an 11-play drive. Then, a 31-yard pass to Lofton helped set up the touchdown for Barkate in their following drive. Barkate entered the game as the team’s second-leading receiver behind Malachi Toney. He had 28 catches for 372 yards and four touchdowns, which were far behind Toney’s otherworldly numbers. But with Toney out, the senior has done his best to step up to the plate for the Hurricanes. He will likely play a crucial role if the Canes’ comeback bid against Notre Dame is going to be successful or not. item.title: Miami incomplete pass controversy: Hurricanes miss out on game-tying TD vs. Notre Dame due to questionable call
item.description: Miami incomplete pass controversy: Hurricanes miss out on game-tying TD vs. Notre Dame due to questionable call originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It's only fitting that we had a controversial call in the end zone during the 2026 edition of the Miami-Notre Dame rivalry, right? Miami's offense, which was playing without star receiver Malachi Toney on the road against Notre Dame, struggled in the beginning. But it started to find its groove in the second half. The Canes scored 21 points in the second half, but a controversial call in the fourth quarter may have taken a game-tying touchdown off the board. Miami quarterback Darian Mensah hit his receiver Elija Lofton in the end zone, but the pass was called incomplete. Here's everything you need to know about the play. MORE: How Miami ruled the 1980s and embraced villain role against Notre Dame Miami incomplete pass controversy Miami's offense struggled in the first half, managing just a field goal, and trailed 17-3 at halftime. But Mensah and the Canes started to find their groove in the second half, as they had three touchdown drives, while the defense started to get stops against CJ Carr and Notre Dame's offense. The Canes made it a one-score game with 9:53 left as Mensah found Cooper Barkate for a touchdown. Notre Dame's Spencer Porath then missed a 53-yard field goal to give Miami the ball back with 3:31 left. Mensah quickly got the offense deep into Notre Dame territory thanks to a 41-yard strike to Elija Lofton. Mensah then had two incompletions after a second down to set up a crucial 4th-and-6. On the play, Mensah threw a pass to Lofton in the end zone. Lofton appeared to initially haul it in, but bobbled it as he went out of bounds. Elijah Lofton couldnt hold it Notre Dame big 4th down stop pic.twitter.com/hXiEXZgvVS — wok (@wokdior) November 8, 2026 The officials called the pass incomplete on the field. Officials reviewed the play, and the NBC broadcast stated that it was an ACC officiating crew on the call. The call was upheld as incomplete, although fans were hoping it would have been a touchdown: Miami was THIS CLOSE to tying things up against Notre Dame. Elija Lofton can't secure the catch and the Hurricanes turn the ball over on downs. pic.twitter.com/yk3IaSGI75 — Underdog CFB (@UnderdogCFB) November 8, 2026 MORE: Notre Dame keeps CFP hopes alive win win over Miami Did officials get the incomplete pass call right? Because Lofton did not maintain control while he completed the process of making the catch, the call was ruled incomplete. There is also the "football move" part of the catch here in-play, which Lofton attempted to make before the ball came out. Here's what the NCAA rulebook says regarding what constitutes as a catch: To catch a ball means that a player: 1. Secures firm control with the hand(s) or arm(s) of a live ball in flight before the ball touches the ground, and 2. Touches the ground inbounds with an

item.title: Georgia 42, Ole Miss 7: ‘Dawgs Turn the Rebs Every Way But Loose
item.description: OXFORD, MISSISSIPPI - NOVEMBER 07: Talyn Taylor #1 of the Georgia Bulldogs reacts after scoring a touchdown during the first half against the Mississippi Rebels at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Oxford, Mississippi. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kirby Smart spent an entire week ruminating on how calm and steady Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss has been this season. He then conspired with Glenn Schumann to put Chambliss in a blender and switch back and forth between the puree and smoothie settings for an entire college football game. Georgia pressured Chambliss early and often, using unconventional pressure from all over the field to confuse the Rebel pass protection and discombobulate Chambliss. The result was an Ole Miss offense that looked like an Ole Mess for most of a 35-7 beatdown. Pete Golding’s team went three and out on their first drive, then only ran four plays on their second. By the time they finally put together anything that looked like a drive they were already down 14-0. The Bulldogs exploded out to that lead by running the dang ball. Nate Frazier took the first snap of the night for the UGA offense for a 46 yard gain deep into Ole Miss territory then the Dawgs just kept pounding the rock, grinding for 127 rushing yards by the end of the first quarter. . The Red and Black would finish the night with a season-high 296 yards on the ground, led by Frazier’s 106 yards on 17 carries. Then Mike Bobo just continued to unload his bag of tricks. An Ole Miss defense that has struggled to avoid giving up big plays found itself doing what it couldn’t do if it hoped to stay in this one: give up a series of big plays. A lot of those big plays had Talyn Taylor’s name all over them. It was a career night for the sophomore receiver, who finished with 4 catches for 140 yards, including touchdown catches of 58 and 65 yards. Crucially, Mike Bobo resisted the urge to get conservative offensively once the Classic City Canines went up by two scores, and it was beautiful to see. The defense however was the story of the night. They harassed Chambliss, forcing him into two turnovers and an uncharacteristically pedestrian stat line.The Rebel signal caller finished 18 of 34 passing for 170 yards and no touchdown passes. Critically however the Dawgs also crushed the Mississippi run game, allowing only 66 yards on the ground on 31 attempts. That total, as well as the Rebs’ 252 yards of total offense, were both season lows. The Red and Black did the things you have to do to win on the road in the SEC: start fast, create turnovers, run the football, and take advantage of scoring opportunities. If you can find something to dislike about this game, you’re a more Munsonian fan than I. That was a violent work of art. The Bulldogs now return to Athens to take on a Missouri team coming off a tough luck loss to Texas. It should be another statement opportunity for Kirby Smart’s team. Until later… Go ‘ Dawgs! !!

item.title: College football winners and losers: Are teams like LSU, Ole Miss and Ohio State now out of the playoff race?
item.description: Saturday showed exactly why there was no need to overreact to the first set of College Football Playoff rankings. Week 10 brought us six matchups between teams in the top 20 of the initial rankings. And when you throw in Ohio State's upset loss at home to Oregon, seven teams with legitimate playoff hopes lost this weekend. And of those seven, only No. 1 Miami can consider its playoff hopes still relatively safe. The other six teams that didn't win all suffered either their second or third defeats. It's highly likely that a 9-3 team or two will make the final 12-team playoff at the end of the season. But for the four contenders that just suffered their third loss, their wiggle room is gone with three weeks to go in the regular season. Don't be surprised if just one or two of the teams listed below end up having a chance to play for the national title. No. 18 Missouri (6-3) Games remaining: at No. 2 Georgia, vs. No. 6 Kentucky, vs. Oklahoma Saturday's result: Lost 34-20 to No. 7 Texas We'll start with a team that we think has the smallest chance of getting to the playoff of any of the top-20 teams who lost on Saturday. The Tigers were a certain playoff team at 10-2 and can still make the playoff at 9-3. But the odds of Missouri heading to Georgia and beating the Bulldogs are very slim, especially after the way the Tigers failed to capitalize in that loss to Texas. Yes, a lot of close replays went against Mizzou. But the Tigers also missed two field goals and had a grand total of 16 yards on their four drives after Texas tied the game at 20-20. No. 14 LSU (6-3) Games remaining : vs. No. 7 Texas, at No. 13 Tennessee, at Arkansas Saturday's result: Lost 31-13 to No. 5 Alabama Do you trust these Tigers to win their remaining three games? A win over Alabama would have allowed LSU to likely be in the playoff with a split of the games against UT-abbreviated teams and a win over Arkansas. Now, LSU needs to beat both Texas and Tennessee. Those wins could be enough to get LSU into the playoff at 9-3, especially if that win comes over Texas. But if those games are losses? LSU is staring at a 7-5 campaign. And that's hardly what anyone had in mind after the school and the state lured Lane Kiffin to Baton Rouge. BATON ROUGE, LA - NOVEMBER 7: Lane Kiffin head coach of the LSU Tigers on the sideline during the second half of a game against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Tiger Stadium on November 7, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Icon Sportswire via Getty Images No. 12 Ohio State (6-3) Games remaining: vs. Northwestern, at Nebraska, vs. Michigan Saturday's result: Lost 41-28 to No. 23 Oregon Ohio State will be favored to win each of its next three games. But Ohio State is going to need a ton of help to make the playoff at 9-3. While the three-loss SEC teams in the vicinity of Ohio State have ranked opponents remaining on their schedules, the Buckeyes don't. The best case for Ohio State is that it wins out and

item.title: Ted Hurst Faces Bears’ Explosive Pass Defense In Sunday Night Clash
item.description: Jonathan Dyer-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears defense has a glaring hole that Tampa Bay’s rookie wide receiver Ted Hurst can target on Sunday night. On 286 pass attempts by opponents through eight contests, Chicago has allowed 23 completions reaching 20 yards or more. This 8% explosive completion rate ranks 20th in the NFL, according to Yahoo Sports . Opponents have also gained 6.01 yards, the second-highest total in the league. The numbers indicate trouble for a unit that prides itself on physical play. Ted Hurst has the tools needed to address this vulnerability. He stands 6-foot-4 and possesses the speed to stretch the field vertically. This season, the rookie has caught 11 passes totaling 168 yards plus one touchdown. His average of 15.3 yards per catch shows he can make big plays when the ball is in the air. His longest reception is 40 yards, proving he can go deep. While he has gone without a reception in the last two games, those were low-volume passing games against Carolina and Atlanta. The Buccaneers attempted just 12 passes against the Panthers and three against the Falcons. Opportunity for a Breakout Sunday Night Football offers Hurst a prime stage to prove his worth against a struggling secondary. Offensive coordinator Zac Robinson knows the Bears allow big plays and will likely design calls to exploit this. Baker Mayfield needs opportunities to take calculated shots downfield to move the chains. Although the Buccaneers have relied heavily on their run game lately, vertical routes and play action might surprise Chicago. Even if Hurst is not the primary target, his size creates matchup problems for Bears cornerbacks. Robinson can use his speed to attack the deep middle of the field. The Bears have been productive in several defensive areas, but they cannot stop the big pass. This weakness gives Tampa Bay a clear path to score points in the red zone. If the Buccaneers can establish the run first, the play action will open up lanes for Hurst to catch the ball in stride. Defensive Line Moves While the offense looks to attack, the Bears are looking to fix their own defensive line. Next week, former Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jordan Elliott is scheduled to take part in a team workout, according to Yahoo Sports. This comes after head coach Ben Johnson indicated that Kentavius Street is “unlikely” to return this season. Elliott has made 65 career starts while amassing 159 tackles, 11 TFLs and 5 sacks. Tennessee head coach Robert Saleh has been an advocate for Elliott despite his recent release. Saleh addressed the gun-related incident that led to Elliott’s departure by calling it a “terrible lapse in judgment.” He said, “I’ll tell you everything you need to know about him. He’s a good man.” Saleh also added that he would be willing to recommend Elliott to other teams looking for defensive line help. Chicago must balance Elliott’s experience with the context of his exit. The team already invested heavily at defensive tackle with Jeffery

item.title: ‘This Is Incredible,’ ‘Made Me Smile’ — CFB Fans Elated as Utah HC Morgan Scalley Improbably Gets His Stolen Helmet Back After 22 Years
item.description: Nov 7, 2026; Salt Lake City, Utah, USA; Utah Utes head coach Morgan Scalley stands on the sideline during the second half against the Brigham Young Cougars at Rice-Eccles Stadium. © Rob Gray-Imagn Images Morgan Scalley remembered the Tostitos flying through the air and the fans pouring onto the field. He remembered beating BYU with a trip to the Fiesta Bowl on the line. The one thing he couldn’t tell you about that night in 2004 was where his helmet went. Then, two days after he brought it up at a press conference, his neighbor knocked on the door. Morgan Scalley’s Neighbor Returns the Helmet 22 Years Later Scalley was asked Monday to pick a favorite memory from the Utah–BYU rivalry. The 2004 game was an easy choice. The Utes beat BYU 52–21 at Rice-Eccles Stadium to finish the regular season 11-0. Scalley, a senior safety who earned Mountain West Defensive Player of the Year honors that season, had to get a replacement helmet after the celebration. “That was my one helmet,” he said. On Wednesday, Scalley’s neighbor Rick showed up with the original. The two had been neighbors for 12 years. Rick told Scalley he was the one who took it during the celebration 22 years earlier, ESPN sideline reporter Taylor McGregor reported . McGregor called it the “Best story this week.” Considering she was covering a top-10 rivalry game, there was some competition. There’s a reason the helmet meant more than a souvenir from a rivalry win. That Utah team became the first from outside the BCS conferences to qualify for a BCS bowl. The Utes went on to beat Pittsburgh 35–7 in the Fiesta Bowl and finish 12-0. For years, Scalley could tell you how the team got there and what happened once it arrived in Tempe. The missing helmet was the loose end. College Football Fans Lap Up Scalley’s Story “This is incredible,” one fan wrote . “Amazing,” sports radio host Sean O’Connell added . Another commenter got a kick out of how long Rick had kept the story to himself. “This is such an insane story! Never being able to tell anybody that you had Morgan Scalley’s 2004 helmet. Welp… now you can,” the commenter wrote . “This is the good stuff…” another commenter wrote . Saturday’s game gave Utah fans plenty to talk about on its own. No. 3 Utah trailed No. 9 BYU 20–14 at halftime, then held the Cougars scoreless the rest of the way. Devon Dampier accounted for all four Utah touchdowns in the 28–20 win over BYU . The Utes are 9-0 for only the third time in program history. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Notre Dame still alive in CFP race after holding off rally from No. 1 Miami
item.description: SOUTH BEND, IN – Notre Dame buckled late Saturday night inside Notre Dame Stadium in the shadow of Touchdown Jesus. The Irish never folded, and now they can buckle up for an altogether different reason: A return trip to the College Football Playoff . Building a three-touchdown lead and then hanging on, the Fighting Irish outlasted Miami 31-24 for the program's first win against a No. 1 team since Clemson was defeated here in 2020. The Fighting Irish , No. 6 in the US LBM Coaches Poll but just No. 11 last Tuesday in the initial College Football Playoff rankings, seemed on the verge of blowing out the Hurricanes. Scoring just moments before the half when CJ Carr connected on play action to Micah Gilbert as he darted into the end zone for a 17-3 halftime lead. Then, Notre Dame got another Gilbert touchdown three minutes into the second half. The Irish defense snuffed out Miami’s opening possession, Jordan Faison delivered a short field with a 56-yard punt return and three snaps later, Gilbert gathered Carr’s third scoring toss for a 21-point lead. The Hurricanes answered – and in a hurry. In less than three minutes of game clock, as the Notre Dame offense lulled its way through the third quarter, Miami got back-to-back touchdown passes from Heisman Trophy candidate Darian Mensah. The teams would trade touchdowns before Miami drove deep into Notre Dame territory late in the fourth quarter. Mensah's pass on fourth down appeared to be caught by tight end Elijah Lofton in the end zone but the ball was knocked out of his hands by defense back Luke Talich before he completely secured it. The play by Talich put the Fighting Irish in position to ice the game with a pair of first downs. They got one, but Miami stiffened and got the ball back with one minute left. Notre Dame sacked Mensah and then tackled him on a run before a first down as the clocked ticked down. The Hurricanes were 62 yards from the end zone with one snap left. The game ended with a series of laterals that failed to go forward, setting off a celebration at midfield with the fans joining the players in a win that helped erase the pain of missing the playoff last year when the final spot went to Miami due to their head-to-head win the season opener. Notre Dame wholly dominated the game’s opening 16 minutes, when it possessed the ball for almost 12 minutes and used Carr’s connection to a toe-tapping Jordan Faison for a 10-0 lead. The Hurricanes almost mounted a meaningful answer, when they drove 83 yards – but failed to gain the final yard. This, after twice getting first-and-goal situations courtesy Notre Dame defensive penalties – the latter setting up the visitors with first-and-goal from the 1. After Boubacar Traore detonated Mensah at the 2-yard line on third-and-goal, Mario Cristobal elected for a field goal. Notre Dame would add a touchdown as Carr found Gilbert for a 18-yard score with 29 seconds left in a half it dominated. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Notre Dame st

item.title: Here's our stars from major Notre Dame win over Miami (FL)
item.description: No. 6 Notre Dame beat No, 1 Miami (FL) 31-24 in a nail-biter that came down to the final play on Saturday. The Fighting Irish were in control in the first half before the Hurricanes punched back in the second half. Notre Dame hung on for the win, which might've been necessary to keep its playoff hopes alive. Here now are the five Notre Dame stars from the game. 5 ⭐️ - CJ Carr I went back and forth on where to put Carr -- he and wide receiver Micah Gilbert were duking it out. I'll give the final nod to Carr, who finished 29-of-40 for 319 yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions. 4 ⭐️ - Micah Gilbert Gilbert had a huge night, with two receiving touchdowns , nine catches for 98 yards, and a long of 20 yards . 3 ⭐️ - Jordan Faison The reliable wide receiver had a huge 56-yard punt return, a touchdown , and six catches for 77 yards, with a long of 27. 2 ⭐️ - Nolan James Jr. James continues to seal the starting role, with a touchdown and several key runs, plus a huge 36-yard pass reception. 1 ⭐️ - Luke Talich Talich's interception made for a major momentum swing , and he knocked the ball loose on what looked like a possible game-tying touchdown for the Hurricanes. He also had six tackles, four of which were solo. item.title: U17WWC: You’ve written your names in gold – Tinubu tells Flamingos
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Nigeria’s Flamingos for making history as the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup following their 2-1 victory over Japan in Saturday’s final in Rabat, Morocco. The president, who received the cheering news upon his return from campaign engagements in Akwa Ibom and Rivers States, hailed Nigeria’s maiden triumph as a proud moment for the nation and a landmark achievement for African women’s football. “What wonderful news to return home to! Our young girls have conquered the world and given Nigerians everywhere another reason to celebrate our great country. “To our gallant Flamingos, I say congratulations. You have shown courage, discipline, determination, and the Nigerian spirit of never giving up. “I followed your journey throughout this tournament, and after your semi-final victory, you promised to bring the trophy home. Today, you have kept that promise. You believed in yourselves, fought for one another, and carried our nation’s flag to the very top of the world. “Your victory is an inspiration to millions of young Nigerian girls who dream of achieving greatness. You have shown them that with hard work, opportunity, and determination, they too can reach the highest levels of achievement. “Today, Nigeria celebrates you. You have written your names in gold, and your country is immensely proud of you.” The president particularly applauds Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku, whose goals secured the historic victory, while commending the entire squad for their exceptional teamwork throughout the tournament. He also congratulates the coaching crew, the Nigeria Football Federation, and the National Sports Commission for their contributions to the team’s success. President Tinubu reaffirms his administration’s commitment to investing in grassroots sports development and expanding opportunities for young Nigerians, particularly girls, to discover, nurture, and fulfill their potential. “Congratulations once again, Flamingos. Thank you for making Nigeria proud.” The post U17WWC: You’ve written your names in gold – Tinubu tells Flamingos appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Rumbling in yoruba land: There’s only one Afenifere despite alleged breakup plan – Secretary
item.description: • Says Adebanjo endorsed Peter Obi in 2023 without telling anybody • Explains how Fasoranti endorsed Tinubu for president despite supplanting his leadership By Dapo Akinrefon Chief Ademola Folarin, a lawyer, is the General Secretary of the pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere. Folarin, who is the Agbaakin Maiyegun of Ibadanland, in this interview, speaks on the leadership crisis in Afenifere, reconciliation in the group, and the decision of the Yoruba body to endorse President Bola Tinubu for 2027 among other issues. Excerpts: There have been issues in the polity ahead of 2027, parties have been trading accusations; there is mudslinging. Do you think this is healthy for our democracy? Look, adversarial politics is one of the hallmarks of democracy. You have to destroy one party in order for you to rise. It’s one of the pitfalls of democracy that we can’t avoid, which is why some people say democracy is not the best form of government. But we haven’t found a better one. I think we are just being dishonest. There is a better one, it’s not necessarily democratic. We can see it in China, we can see it in the Gulf states, a combination of constitutionalism and monarchy. In China, there is no monarchy, but they have a system of evolutionary leadership, and it is working. The trouble spots in the world are the democracies. Just look around you, everywhere you see a problem, it’s democratic. That’s because it has to be like that. If you want to see the downfall of someone to rise, you can’t have peace, you can’t have stability. The bastion of democracy, Europe and America, are on the decline. It’s consistent with the aims and objectives of the founding fathers of democracy. It was foreseen, but it was unavoidable. If you choose your leaders based purely on numbers, you cannot avoid obvious mistakes. In our country, with the presidential system, it is the same in America. We have simply imported a corrupt system here, presidential system. If you don’t have money, you can’t do anything. That’s what you have. Mudslinging, everything is part of it. Nigeria has practised the parliamentary system before. Now, it’s practising the presidential system. Which do you think Nigeria can adopt? Do you think it should jettison the two and have another system of government? It’s a no-brainer which one should prefer between the Westminster parliamentary system and the presidential system. The Westminster parliamentary system is far cheaper and far more representative. Why do I say so? If I want to be prime minister, I don’t need to do a national campaign or whatever. I go to Eti-Osa local government, campaign and win there. Once I win there and my party wins the majority of seats in parliament, I form government. But in presidential, I have to win the majority of votes in the entire country. item.title: ADC judgment could cause civil war if not properly managed—Amaechi
item.description: …Says mistake I made in 2023 was listening to Buhari By Olayinka Ajayi Vice presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Mr Rotimi Amaechi, has warned that the Federal High Court judgment against the leadership of his party could trigger unrest. Last Thursday, the Federal High Court in Abuja nullified the National Working Committee led by former Senate President, David Mark, in a ruling that also invalidated the process that produced former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as the party’s presidential candidate for the 2027 elections. The judgment, delivered by Justice Peter Lifu, also nullified the emergence of former Minister of Interior, Rauf Aregbesola, as National Secretary, and other decisions taken by the Mark-led leadership, including the nomination of candidates for elective offices. The court further ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, not to recognise or act on decisions taken at the party’s 99th National Executive Committee meeting of July 27, 2025. The judgment followed a suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, filed by former ADC Deputy National Chairman (North-East), Nafiu Gombe, who challenged the process through which Mark and other members of the caretaker committee assumed control of the party. Speaking in an interview on Mainland 98.3fm, Amaechi said: “It could cause a civil war if not properly managed. When we heard the news, we quickly met, myself and the presidential candidate and the chairman of the party, and we said: ‘please, lower the tempo’. I am not alleging, as there is a document signed by Nafiu resigning at the same time as Ralph Nwosu. There is a video of him behind David Mark handing over to David Mark. They go to hire, pay money, go to court and compromise some system here and there. There is no internal rift in our party, none. It is just the fear of the All Progressives Congress, APC. When they saw what happened in Sokoto, they began to cause a crisis that would frighten voters. Looking at things, which other party is opposing the APC other than ADC? The president is from the South-West, and we have three other presidential candidates in the South-West. Even if they don’t get every vote, they would certainly get some votes, and don’t forget the governor of Oyo State, Seyi Makinde, is also running. Let us assume he fails everywhere in the South-West; he will not fail in Oyo, where he comes from. Assuming he wins Oyo State, that is minus one for Tinubu. There is another presidential candidate from the South-East (Peter Obi) who will take away five states from the South-East. Already, he has lost six states from the South. The battle is in the South-South; I am their son. I am running as a vice presidential candidate. Here is a man called Atiku Abubakar, running alone in the North with 19 Northern states.” On how he lost the 2023 APC presidential primaries to President Tinubu, he said: “Anybody would have defeated anybody. item.title: 68 days to polls: Struggling Nigerians make 2027 demands
item.description: • Send strong messages to Tinubu, Atiku, Obi, Makinde, Adebayo, Donald Duke, others • Affordability, security, steady power supply top list By Steve Oko, Olasukanmi Akoni, Esther Onyegbula, Cynthia Alo, Shina Abubakar, Rotimi Ojomoyela, Golok Nanmwa, James Ogunnaike, Musa Ubandawaki, Peter Duru, Haruna Aliyu, Deola Badru & Chiamaka Ekwuwe Hunger is biting harder, insecurity is spreading fear across communities, businesses are groaning under the weight of rising energy costs, and millions of Nigerians are struggling to survive on incomes that can hardly meet their basic needs. From the farmer afraid of returning to his farm to the unemployed graduate searching endlessly for a job, the average Nigerian is looking towards the 2027 general elections, with 68 days to the polls, with one overriding expectation: a president who will make life worth living again. With the political atmosphere charged ahead of the presidential election, Nigerians across the country have sent a strong message to the presidential candidates: the next occupant of Aso Rock must move beyond campaign rhetoric and confront hunger, poverty, insecurity, unemployment, inflation and the worsening living conditions of citizens. Expectations The expectations are particularly high as President Bola Ahmed Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC) seeks another mandate, facing an array of contenders, including former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC); former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC); Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM); Senator Sandy Ojang Onor of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP); former Cross River State Governor, Donald Duke, of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP); Omoyele Sowore of the African Action Congress (AAC); and Adewole Adebayo of the Social Democratic Party (SDP). Other candidates on the Independent National Electoral Commission’s published list include Sunday Chibuzo Okereke of the Labour Party (LP), Rufai Adekunle Omo-Aje of the Action Alliance (AA), Abbas-Bin Aliyu of the Action Democratic Party (ADP), Yusuf Kabiru of the Allied Peoples Party (APP), Sunday Adenuga of the Boot Party (BP), Moses Olusoji Adebisi of the Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA), Ada Elizabeth Frederick Okwori of the National Democratic Party (NDP), Nkem Esther Okereke of the National Rescue Movement (NRM), Peter Ada Agada of the Young Progressives Party (YPP) and Daniel Daberechukwu Nwanyanwu of the Zenith Labour Party (ZLP). Survival Beyond the political parties, personalities and permutations surrounding the election, those who spoke to Sunday Vanguard in this public opinion survey said their concerns are fundamentally about survival, dignity and a better future.
