item.title: 2027: Ask Atiku where he got money to build university
item.description: •Shettima hits Obi •Yari targets 2.3m votes in Rivers •President will get 3m votes — Fubara By Henry Umoru, Omeiza Ajayi and Daniel Abia President Bola Tinubu yesterday challenged Nigerians to ask former Vice President Atiku Abubakar how he acquired the money to establish his university while serving in government, accusing him of using public resources to advance private interests. Tinubu, who spoke at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally, held at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium, Port Harcourt, Rivers State, also thanked Governor Siminalayi Fubara for his handling of the political crisis in the state, assuring him that he would not regret supporting him (Tinubu). The President, who is seeking a second term in the January 16, 2027 presidential election, urged Rivers residents to renew the mandate they gave him and Vice President Kashim Shettima in 2023. He also praised the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, for his development efforts and political support, describing him as a dependable partner in his administration. Taking a swipe at opposition politicians who have criticised his government’s handling of the economy, particularly the rising cost of living and hardship, Tinubu said those accusing his administration of creating hunger were responsible for the problems they now complain about. “Those people, talking of hunger, are clearly the mess they created. Atiku was one of them,” he said.\ “Ask him how he built the university, while he was in office as vice president in charge of our economy. Who built the university for you? It’s your money. It’s your effort. A man without moral integrity, rectitude and ethics for the office,” Tinubu said. The President’s remarks came amid renewed political exchanges between the ruling party and opposition figures ahead of the 2027 general election. Tinubu also used the occasion to express appreciation to Fubara for maintaining peace in Rivers State following the political confrontation that had threatened the stability of the state government. “I want to thank you specifically, for your maturity, understanding, respect for the wisdom of elders. When we intervened, you respected our position. You maintained peace. You are a committed democrat. Fubara, you will not regret what you have done,” he said. Recalling the support Rivers State gave him during the 2023 presidential election, Tinubu said the people stood by him at a time when his political fortunes appeared uncertain. “Rivers State, you have been good to me. In 2023, when I looked very helpless, you stood out to support me. Today again, I return here to say thank you. And seek your support for the second term,” he said. He specifically acknowledged Wike’s contribution to his administration, describing the former Rivers governor as a development partner whose work in the FCT had earned him recognition. “He is already a development partner of a Bola Ahmed Tinubu administration. item.title: Institutional Memory, Professional Knowledge and the CORFEPS Journal
item.description: By Tunji Olaopa The Council of Retired Federal Permanent Secretaries (CORFEPS) is an association of patriotic former public servants that embodies administrative experiences, institutional memories and professional knowledge that could pull a lot of political and administrative weight within the reform imperative to transform governance architecture, the civil service and its ecosystem. As a multidisciplinary body of retired public servants with vast knowledge of the workings of the system, CORFEPS possesses a huge significance in connecting the institutional and reform dots in terms of where the civil service system is coming from, where it is at the moment and where it intends to be, given the democratic imperatives and development necessities of the current Tinubu administration. It is one of the most critical stakeholders in the public administration communities of practice and service that articulates a continuing professional and institutional interest in furthering the relevance of the civil service as a significant player in the development process in Nigeria. The necessity of such a body derives from the fact that patriotic and meritorious service does not need to end with retirement. Indeed, more can still be done in entrenching the institutional memories that retired permanent secretaries embody. CORFEPS, under the able chairmanship of Mahmud Yayale Ahmed, has been energetic in its consistent push to regain the vocational honor, professional ethos and administrative efficiency of the civil service. And in furtherance of this enthusiastic push for the significance of the civil service system as one critical cornerstone of democratic governance in Nigeria, CORFEPS has just launched an amazing initiative: the CORFEPS Journal on Pubic Policy and Governance. This significant initiative must be situated within a larger context of the institutional reform of the civil service system, especially its status as a value-based institution founded on merit, public spiritedness and professionalism. That context facilitates a framework that allows the past and the present to initiate conversation, and for both retired and current public servants to incessantly brainstorm the future of the bureaucratic system and its capability readiness to shoulder the burden of public policy implementation. The journal, I must say, presses the advantage of escalating the fundamental significance of professional knowledge and its role in deepening institutional progress. In other words, through it, CORFEPS provides a rare forum—draw, I dare say, from the administrative history of that golden era when administrative theorists (the gown) and practitioners (the town) were in conversation—within which administrative ideas, practices and initiatives could be discussed, extended and applied. The inaugural edition of the CORFEPS journal is indeed a full, rich and exciting package that is sufficiently exciting to signal to the communities of service and practice that somethi

item.title: AMERICA IS NOT NIGERIA: Why Trump’s midterm defeat cannot predict Tinubu’s 2027 fortunes
item.description: By Kayode Akinmade The sweeping defeat suffered by President Donald Trump’s Republican Party in the November 3 American midterm elections has predictably provided fresh ammunition for Nigeria’s opposition politicians, who are already attempting to draw parallels between the political fortunes of the American president and those of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general elections. While the comparison may offer an attractive political talking point, it is, at best, superficial and, at worst, a deliberate attempt to transplant the political circumstances of one country into another. There is no doubt that the Republican defeat represents a significant setback for Trump. Democrats secured control of both chambers of Congress, delivering a powerful electoral rebuke to the Republican administration and signalling widespread dissatisfaction with some of its policies. The result has opened a new chapter in American politics and raised questions about the direction of Trump’s presidency. However, the critical question is whether the circumstances that produced this outcome in the United States are sufficiently comparable to Nigeria’s political and economic realities to justify the conclusion that Tinubu is destined for a similar electoral fate in 2027. The answer is no. America is not Nigeria. Trump is not Tinubu. And the political dynamics of the United States cannot be mechanically imported into Nigeria’s electoral calculations. Indeed, one of the most important factors behind the Republican Party’s defeat was the controversial war involving the United States and Iran, a foreign policy decision that has generated enormous economic, diplomatic and security consequences for the Trump administration. The conflict, which has lasted several months, has heightened concerns about American military involvement abroad, increased pressure on energy markets and contributed to rising fuel prices. For American households already grappling with the cost of living, the war became another source of economic anxiety. Its financial implications, military casualties and uncertain strategic objectives also generated questions about the wisdom of the administration’s foreign policy choices. Iran conflict Significantly, the political consequences were acknowledged by the highest levels of the American government. Trump admitted that the Iran conflict contributed to his party’s electoral difficulties, although he maintained that the military action was necessary. His Vice President, JD Vance, was considerably more direct, declaring that “the reason we lost is the war.” That admission is particularly instructive. It establishes that the Republican defeat was not simply an abstract expression of public dissatisfaction with a sitting president. It was substantially connected to identifiable policy decisions and their consequences for American voters. The question, therefore, is why Nigeria’s opposition should expect the political consequences of Trump’s dec

item.title: Countdown to 2027: Edo North is for Oshiomhole
item.description: By Allison Abanum Adams Oshiomhole’s first term has been defined by a deliberate strategy of translating legislative power into tangible federal presence for Edo North. As Chairman of the Senate Committee on Interior, he has leveraged his position to facilitate federal employment for constituents and ensure fair representation in federal institutions. His legislative record includes moving over 10 motions and sponsoring many bills. These are not abstract motions; they are institutional investments that will outlast any single political cycle. On the ground, Oshiomhole constituency interventions have reached all wards in Edo North, a coverage rate that speaks to both reach and intentionality. Oshiomhole has moved from delivering roads to delivering accountability, and Edo North have seen the difference in both bricks and budgets. Beyond infrastructure, his engagement with youth leaders and traditional rulers signals a recognition that representation must be relational, not transactional, a point underscored by his refusal to charge constituents for assistance and his warning against extortion in his name. The political consolidation around Oshiomhole 2027 bid reflects a broader strategic calculation within Edo North. Endorsements have since crossed traditional lines: From the market women in Auchi to the Artisan in Iyahmo, down to all the student bodies and community leaders, it is clear that it is no longer a question of whether Edo North is standing for Oshiomhole; it is a question of how loudly Edo North will say so. To the people in the rural areas of Edo North, they have risen from service, unity, and discipline: delivery that touches households, reconciliation that silences internal friction, and grassroots organisation that turns intention into votes. The good people of Edo North on their own are moving ward by ward to get support for Oshiomhole. The plough is heavy; the hands must be steady because the furrow ahead is 2027. The message is clear: no retreat, no sideways glance, no nostalgia for old battles in Edo North. A senatorial district that has seen the light and future must now prove it can cultivate it, row by row, ward by ward, state by state, until the harvest of triumph is achieved. Every leader, every member, every supporter keeps eyes on the furrow, not on the noise. So, let the word go forth: APC is on the plough, and there is no looking back until Oshiomhole is sent back to the Senate in 2027. The task is not to boast of yesterday but to labour for tomorrow with humility, focus, and determination. The harvest belongs to those who keep ploughing. For a senatorial district that has historically oscillated between alignment and agitation, the emerging consensus is that Oshiomhole federal network is an asset too valuable to surrender. Abanum lives in Abuja. The post Countdown to 2027: Edo North is for Oshiomhole appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: A Ballot on a Burial Date? Northern Nigeria Confronts the Symbolism of January 16
item.description: By Hassan A Karofi The choice of dates in politics is often presented as a matter of administrative convenience. Yet history teaches us that dates carry powerful symbolism, especially in societies where collective memories of tragedy and triumph remain deeply rooted. As Nigeria prepares for a presidential election scheduled for January 16, 2026, it is important to reflect on what that date means to millions of people, particularly in Northern Nigeria, where January 16 is associated with one of the darkest episodes in the country’s history. The significance of January 16 cannot be understood without revisiting the events of the country’s first military coup. In the early hours of January 15, 1966, a group of young military officers launched Nigeria’s first coup d’état. By the morning of January 16, the consequences of the coup were evident. Several of Nigeria’s most prominent political and military leaders had been assassinated. Among those killed were Sir Ahmadu Bello, the Sardauna of Sokoto and Premier of Northern Nigeria; Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, Nigeria’s first Prime Minister; Brigadier Samuel Ademulegun; Brigadier Zakariya Maimalari; and other senior political and military figures. While leaders from different regions were affected, the perception in the North was that the coup disproportionately targeted Northern political leadership. This perception would profoundly shape political attitudes and inter-ethnic relations for decades. The events following the coup further deepened Northern grievances. Major General Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi assumed power and suspended parts of the constitutional order. In many parts of Northern Nigeria, suspicion and anger grew rapidly, culminating in the counter-coup of July 1966. The resulting instability ultimately contributed to the chain of events that led to the Nigerian Civil War. More than six decades later, the memory of January 1966 remains alive. For many Northern families, historians, traditional institutions, and political observers, January 16 is not merely another date on the calendar. It is a reminder of a traumatic turning point that altered Nigeria’s political trajectory and claimed the lives of leaders who continue to be revered across the region. Against this backdrop, the decision to hold a presidential election on January 16 raises legitimate questions. Whether the date was chosen for logistical, constitutional, or electoral reasons, policymakers should recognize that symbolism matters in politics. Elections are national events meant to unite citizens around a shared democratic purpose. When an election coincides with a date associated with historical mourning for a significant section of the country, there is a risk that the symbolism overshadows the democratic exercise itself. This concern is not necessarily about rejecting the election or questioning its legitimacy. Rather, it is about understanding how political decisions are perceived. item.title: 2027: Between Okowa and Ochei, a Trojan horse race?
item.description: By Emmanuel l. Nwagboniwe Let’s not equivocate here. The indices and optics in the political space amply suggest that the electoral race to represent Delta North in the Senate in 2027 is a direct contest between the former Delta State Governor, Dr. Ifeanyi Okowa of the All Progressives Congress (APC ), and ex -Speaker of the Delta State House of Assembly, Victor Ochei of the National Democratic Party (NDC). Evidently, the projection of a contest likely to throw up soap- box rhetoric, anxieties, euphoria, and political high drama, horse trading, and possibly, mudslinging, is a no-brainer: Okowa and Ochei have bounced into the political ring with unequalled superlatives and robust social capital. Commendably too, these former political allies’ ‘roll call of honour’ tells a convincing story of remarkably impressive private and public service careers- years put in and sacrificed largely in selfless and people-centred engagements. For instance, a studied glance at Dr Ifeanyi Okowa’s resume speaks volumes: medical doctor; council chairman; Commissioner of Health; Secretary to the Delta State Government (SSG); Senator of the Federal Republic of Nigeria; two- term Governor of Delta State, ex -Vice Presidential candidate of the People’s Democratic Party (PDP) in the 2023 General Election. Conversely, Victor Ochei is equally a no fresher in the public cum political space. He is a graduate of Chemical Engineering; Founder/ Chairman of Day Notch Nigeria Limited, an engineering firm of global status; Member, Delta State House of Assembly representing Aniocha North Council; Deputy Minority Leader; Speaker, Delta State House of Assembly; Executive Director, Maritime Labour and Cabotage Services at the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NlMASA); President, Nigerian Tennis Federation, among others. Without gas lighting, these political highflyers’ ‘selling points’ make any of them eminently qualified to represent the Anioma nationality in the Red Chamber. However, one knows that making a choice out of these two top contenders, especially by voters in a dynamic and highly unpredictable democratic space like ours where selfish and primordial sentiments hold sway, is certainly a herculean task, yet a candidate’s ‘report card’ remains an added advantage. For Okowa, he is majorly regarded as a grassroots politician who walks his talk in terms of mass mobilisation, especially across the nine councils that make up the Delta North Senatorial District. Evidently too, the former governor’s enduring stay in the political trenches for over three decades tells a reassuring story of one who understands the undercurrents and dynamics of power ‘capture’. Moreover, Okowa has other political assets to take to the electioneering field; he has a vast and extensive experience in the executive and the legislative arms of government, and no matter how hard his traducers knock him, he being an ex -state executive, has a chunk of tangible and verifiable score cards to pr

item.title: FG plans National Sports Commission office in Kwara – Magaji
item.description: By Demola Akinyemi ILORIN – The Federal Government has concluded plans to establish an office of the National Sports Commission (NSC) in Kwara State, following the development of sports facilities by the administration of Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq. The Executive Chairman of the Kwara State Sports Commission, Coach Bola Magaji, disclosed this in Ilorin, saying officials of the NSC had been impressed by the facilities provided by the state government. Magaji spoke at the unveiling of a book titled The Sardauna of Ilorin in the Eyes of History, written in honour of AbdulRazaq, who holds the traditional title of Sardauna of Ilorin. The book was authored by Abiodun Abdul Kareem, a senior journalist and editor of Herald on Sunday, the Sunday publication of the Kwara State Printing and Publishing Corporation. Magaji recalled that officials of the National Sports Commission visited Kwara about three weeks ago to assess the sports facilities developed by the AbdulRazaq administration over the past seven years. He said the officials expressed satisfaction with the facilities at the state stadium complex and indicated that the proposed NSC office would be established in the state. According to him, the development reflects the growing recognition of Kwara’s investment in sports infrastructure. Magaji said the state’s stadium complex could boast of some of the best squash court facilities in the world, adding that Kwara contingents to national and international sporting competitions had recorded improved medal-winning performances. He attributed the development to investments in sports infrastructure and efforts to promote sporting activities in the state. Also speaking, the Special Adviser and Counsellor to the Governor, Alhaji Saad Salahudeen, said AbdulRazaq’s contributions to governance, politics, youth development and national development would continue to attract attention in the years ahead. He said the governor’s footprints in public service would remain relevant and be referenced in the next 50 years. Earlier, the Chairman of the Organising Committee, Mallam Umar Abdulwahab, said the event was designed to provide a platform for discussions on leadership, public service, governance and historical preservation. He said the initiative was also aimed at documenting experiences and inspiring future generations. The event was attended by several dignitaries, including the Emir of Ilorin, Alhaji Ibrahim Sulu-Gambari, who was represented by Magaji Ogundele; Alhaji Saad Kajola; Alhaji Yusuf Abdullahi; the Secretary to the State Government, Professor Mamman Jibril; Senior Adviser on Islamic Religion, Alhaji Ibrahim Danmegoro; and Senior Adviser on Political Communication, Alhaji Bashir Adigun, among others. The post FG plans National Sports Commission office in Kwara – Magaji appeared first on Vanguard News .

A decade after ascending the revered throne, the monarch’s anniversary provides an opportunity to celebrate the enduring institution of the Benin monarchy, reflect on its contributions to cultural preservation and reaffirm the values that have sustained the kingdom across generations. More than a ceremonial commemoration, the anniversary brings together culture, history, sports, intellectual discourse, community engagement and royal pageantry in a programme designed to showcase the richness of Benin heritage. For Eagle Aromatic Schnapps, Nigeria’s Authentic Traditional Prayer Drink, culture is more than a reflection of the past; it is a living heritage that connects generations, reinforces communal identity and preserves the values that define a people. This belief finds meaningful expression in the 10th Coronation Anniversary of His Royal Majesty, Oba Ewuare II, CFR, the Oba of Benin Kingdom. As a brand whose identity is rooted in Nigeria’s traditional heritage, Eagle Aromatic Schnapps recognises the significance of royal institutions as custodians of history, customs and cultural continuity. Its association with this historic milestone reflects the brand’s appreciation of the traditions that have sustained the Benin Kingdom and contributed to Nigeria’s diverse cultural identity. Eagle Aromatic Schnapps identifying with the anniversary goes beyond participating in a royal celebration. It represents an opportunity to reaffirm the importance of cultural preservation, community engagement and respect for the traditional institutions that continue to shape the country’s social fabric. Speaking on the significance of the anniversary, John Bamgbose, Assistant Brand Manager, Schnapps and Gin, Intercontinental Distillers Limited, described the occasion as an opportunity to celebrate the Benin Kingdom’s rich history and the values that connect generations. item.title: 2027: Danladi vows to build on AbdulRazaq’s achievements
item.description: By Demola Akinyemi ILORIN – The governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kwara State, Rt. Hon. Salihu-Yakubu Danladi, has said his seven years of experience in the legislature and familiarity with the state’s development challenges have prepared him to govern the state. Danladi, who is also the Speaker of the Kwara State House of Assembly, pledged to consolidate the achievements of Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq and take the state to greater heights if elected in the 2027 governorship election. He said Kwara needed continuity and further development rather than a return to what he described as its ugly past. The APC candidate spoke during the News Keg, an interactive programme organised by the Kwara State Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), where he discussed his political journey, legislative experience, achievements and development agenda ahead of the 2027 election. Danladi maintained that he was not a political novice, having served as Speaker since 2019 and participated in legislative processes supporting the present administration’s programmes. “I am not new to what is happening in Kwara State today. I have spent seven years in the legislature. No other candidate had any experience in government. I know virtually every sector and the challenges confronting the state,” he said. He argued that his legislative experience had given him a broad understanding of governance, particularly through the House of Assembly’s appropriation and oversight responsibilities, which he said complemented the executive’s implementation of policies and projects. The governorship candidate, an electrical engineering graduate, also highlighted his academic pursuits, disclosing that he had undertaken programmes in revenue management, peace, conflict and security studies and was currently pursuing a PhD in economic development. Reflecting on his representation of Ilesha/Gwanara Constituency, Danladi identified access to potable water, rural roads, healthcare, education and security as some of the major challenges that informed his legislative interventions. He said he facilitated the provision of about 210 boreholes across communities in his constituency during his first term, alongside the construction and rehabilitation of rural roads. One of the projects he highlighted was a 33-kilometre road linking communities in the constituency, which he said had significantly improved movement in the area. According to him, residents previously endured several hours of travelling during the rainy season for journeys that would ordinarily take about 30 minutes. On healthcare, the Speaker said he facilitated interventions in 18 primary healthcare centres and supported efforts to improve existing general and cottage hospitals. He added that his interventions had extended beyond his constituency, noting that his position as Speaker had provided opportunities to support development projects and empowerment programmes in other p

item.title: Receive what you confess, by Funmi Komolafe
item.description: Gradually, year 2026 is drawing to an end. Being alive is a reason we must continuously thank God. Brethren, have you said thank you Jesus this morning? Please do. You owe the Lord gratitude. Beloved, last week we mentioned confession as a key to a miracle. Today, we’ll return to that with more details. I’ll start with an uncommon story of the son of a farmer whose father was regarded as poor in a town. This young boy went to the farm with his father and he saw man drive past them in an exotic car. The boy looked back admired the car and said to himself “ I am going to drive a better car in this town”. That was decades ago, today that boy now a man is perhaps the richest person in that town of course with the best cars in that town but he took some steps. We’ll return to in the article. Brethren, let’s go to the spiritual. The word of the Lord tells us in Proverbs 18 vs. 21 ( NIV) “ the tongue has the power of life and death, and those who love it eat its fruit”. The son of a farmer used his tongue positively and he is eating the fruits of the words that he spoke to himself today. As Christians however, we need not use the tongue casually as the farmer’s son did. We need to use the tongue in line with the word of God. How then do we use the appropriate word? The answer is found in the word of Prophet Joshua in Joshua 1 vs.8: “ Do not let this Book of the Law depart from your mouth; meditate on it day and night, so that you may be careful to do every written in it. Then you will be prosperous and successful”. The importance of tongue that God has given to all human beings is repeated in Psalm 1 vs. 2: “ But his delight is in the law of the LORD, and on his law he meditates day and night”. Just as you need to study to pass an exam you need to study the Word of God to be able to confess it. Confession in this case is not about the sins you have committed but it’s about saying what God has promised you and your desire to have it. To confess it, you need to memorize that particular verse of the Bible and say it to yourself. In other words, you need to put the words you have memorized into action by saying it to yourself and as you do so, if no human being sees you, the invisible God is watching and listening to you. How do I know? I knew a woman that was barren for over 20 years. She learnt the word by going to church regularly and reading the Holy Bible on her own. The first, is Deuteronomy 7 vs. 14: “ You will be blessed more than any other people, none of your men or women will be childless, nor any of your livestock without young”. These two passages are quite relevant for anyone waiting on the Lord for children. item.title: NASA Awards Moon Base Transportation, Technology, Science Projects
item.description: Artist’s concept of living and working at Moon Base. Credit: NASA NASA announced a suite of awards and mission updates on Saturday to expand the agency’s Moon Base exploration, science, and infrastructure capabilities. The investments will advance commercial robotic deliveries, a nuclear-powered rover named PROMISE, launch and orbital transfer services, and surface infrastructure as the agency works with American industry to establish a sustained presence on the Moon’s South Pole. The agency shared the news at the MAX POWER aerospace expo and air show at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. “We are building the Moon Base mission by mission,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “Today’s announcements expand nearly every part of that campaign, using the playbook that carried NASA through its greatest eras: fly often, learn, apply those lessons, and get more better and more capable with every mission. When our astronauts return to the Moon, they will arrive with the first elements of the Moon Base already waiting for them on the surface.” “In the eight months since Ignition, we’ve made incredible strides in accomplishing the near impossible: establishing a permanent outpost on the lunar surface,” said Carlos García-Galán, manager, Moon Base Program. “We’ve consolidated numerous efforts into a streamlined program, evolving our human exploration architecture into an iterative and sustained campaign for Moon Base technology development and implementation. Most importantly, we’ve taken action, awarding new contracts and forging new partnerships to accelerate development.” Moon Base cargo landers To strengthen the cargo lander network needed to support the Moon Base, NASA selected eight companies for the next phase of its CLPS ( Commercial Lunar Payload Services ) initiative. The companies are eligible to compete for future lunar surface delivery missions under the new CLPS 2 contract: Blue Origin Firefly Aerospace Intuitive Machines ispace-U.S. Lockheed Martin Space Northrop Grumman Space Systems SpaceX Voyager Technologies Under the CLPS 2 framework, the companies will provide lunar delivery services, including managing, building, and operating landers that transport NASA science, technology, and infrastructure payloads to the Moon. The CLPS 2 framework is a 10-year, multiple-award, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity master contract with a combined maximum value of $10 billion. NASA increased the value of the current CLPS 1.0 contract from $2.6 billion to $4.2 billion to support initial Phase One Moon Base objectives. The original CLPS contract will remain in place through November 2028, with an additional five-year period to complete awarded lunar deliveries through November 2033. Nuclear-powered Moon rover NASA also announced it is moving forward with development of PROMISE (Polar Rover for Observation, Mapping, and In-Situ Exploration) . item.title: NASA Seeks Next Generation of Explorers to Join Astronaut Corps
item.description: NASA announced its 2025 Astronaut Candidate Class on Sept. 22, 2025, at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Credit: NASA/Helen Arase Vargas NASA is looking for the explorers who will help write the next chapter of human spaceflight. Applications are now open for the agency’s next class of astronauts, who will join NASA as America returns to the Moon, builds the Moon Base, and lays the groundwork for the first crewed missions to Mars. The next generation of astronauts will train to operate on the lunar surface, live and work beyond Earth, and take on missions that will push the boundaries of human exploration farther than ever before. U.S. citizens interested in joining the astronaut corps have until 11:59 p.m. EST Thursday, Dec. 3, to submit their completed application materials at: https://go.nasa.gov/3WyvlQi “This is an extraordinary time to join NASA’s astronaut corps,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “The people we select could walk on the Moon, live and work at the Moon Base, and help pioneer the systems and operations that will ultimately carry crews to Mars. Those missions will demand technical excellence, sound judgment, teamwork, and courage. NASA’s astronaut corps has always called on remarkable Americans willing to take on extraordinary challenges in service to the nation. If you are ready to join that tradition, come help write the next chapter of humanity’s greatest adventure.” NASA expects to make its final selection in late 2027 to begin training as the next class of astronaut candidates. “The window is open. The mission is waiting. And the only thing missing from the greatest adventure humanity has ever embarked upon is you,” said NASA Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson. The agency last opened applications in 2024. From more than 8,000 applications, 10 astronaut candidates were selected in 2025 and are currently completing nearly two years of training. “For those who apply, becoming a NASA astronaut is more than a career opportunity,” said Scott Tingle, chief astronaut and chair of the Astronaut Selection Board at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. “It is a chance to join a legacy of explorers who have pushed the boundaries of discovery and play a role in the missions that will shape humanity’s future in space. The next generation of astronaut candidates could help write history while inspiring future scientists, engineers, and explorers.” Since the 1960s, NASA has selected 370 people to train as astronaut candidates for its increasingly challenging missions. The agency has 32 astronauts active in the astronaut corps, and selected applicants will join their ranks to study spacewalking, lunar geology, operations of high-performance aircraft, and more. The basic requirements to apply include United States citizenship and a master’s degree in a STEM field, including engineering, biological science, physical science, or computer science from an accredited institution. item.title: “When Are You Coming Home?” ValueJet Restores Daily Flights to Asaba Ahead of the Festive Season
item.description: Daily Lagos–Asaba and Asaba–Abuja services resume on Friday, 20 November 2026, strengthening regional connectivity and bringing families together for the holidays. Somewhere in Lagos or Abuja right now, a phone is ringing, and the voice on the other end is asking the single question that marks the true beginning of the Nigerian festive season: “When are you coming home?” For thousands of professionals, business owners, and families whose answer is Asaba and the surrounding communities across Delta and Anambra states, ValueJet has delivered timely news. The airline will officially resume daily scheduled flights on its Lagos–Asaba and Asaba–Abuja routes starting Friday, 20 November 2026, just as year-end travel planning reaches peak momentum. The end of the year carries an undeniable emotional pull back to one’s roots. It is the season of growing gift lists, overpacked suitcases, group chats buzzing with reunion itineraries, and the quiet warmth of returning to familiar streets. For many families, December represents the single period in the year when loved ones assemble under one roof. By reintroducing daily non-stop frequency on both routes, ValueJet provides critical operational flexibility for holiday travelers. Whether passengers are heading home early to spend the entire season with family or flying out closer to Christmas Eve after wrapping up the work year, the restored schedule ensures seamless travel options tailored to diverse holiday schedules. “The festive season is fundamentally about people, relationships, and shared moments. At ValueJet, our mission is to ensure that distance never stands in the way of those connections,” said Omololu Majekodunmi , Managing Director of ValueJet. “Restoring our daily services to Asaba reflects our deep commitment to serving the travel needs of our passengers during the most important time of the year. We are proud to offer a reliable, comfortable, and affordable gateway home for families and communities across the region.” The Lagos–Asaba service bridges Nigeria’s commercial capital directly with the vibrant heart of Delta State, facilitating easy access across the South-South and South-East regions. Simultaneously, the Asaba–Abuja route delivers a direct, hassle-free link between the nation’s capital and Asaba, eliminating lengthy road journeys and complex connection itineraries. The resumption complements ValueJet’s rapidly expanding domestic and regional network. Domestically, the airline provides essential air links to key destinations including Port Harcourt, Jos, Owerri, Calabar, Benin, and GWI-Iperu. Beyond Nigeria’s borders, ValueJet continues to extend its reach beyond established destinations like Accra, Banjul, Cotonou, and Malabo with upcoming regional route expansions to Libreville, Monrovia, and Abidjan. item.description: null On Episode 235 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Rod Pyle are joined by Dr. Jim Green to talk about the past, present, and future of planetary exploration. Robots have, and always will, be the first to go to the dark and scary places in space. For many years, Jim oversaw these missions for NASA as their Chief Scientist. He has always been passionate about NASA's science programs and believes we're quite likely to find life off-Earth in the near future. Join us! item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
item.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
item.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments." item.title: AI broke the cybersecurity world. What’s next?
item.description: Today, I’m talking with Alex Stamos, chief security officer at Cognition and longtime cybersecurity expert, about what a mess cybersecurity is right now. This episode is part one of a special series looking at AI in real life. I’ve always enjoyed talking to Alex because he’s so direct, and you’re going to hear him say that the multibillion-dollar cybersecurity industry as we’ve known it is essentially overdue to the unrelenting, AI-boosted waves of hacks, breaches, and attacks — and this is only the beginning of how much AI is changing security. Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts. Head here . Not a subscriber? You can sign up here . Both private actors and also state actors, like Russia or North Korea, are breaking into systems all over thanks to AI helping them both detect and exploit vulnerabilities all at the same time. It’s got a real frontier feel to it, Alex notes, just like the ’90s, when the whole idea of an always-online world was brand-new. That much disruption means a lot of places where bad guys can get in while everyone else is left scrambling. Alex isn’t a doomer in the long run, but he does think we’re in for a “dark age” while we try to figure out how on earth to adapt to the new era. There’s a lot going on here — we even got all the way to how AI-powered misinformation and slop might be managed on our social networks. Before we get going, do me a favor and subscribe to Decoder on YouTube, where we put out new episodes every Monday and Thursday. Okay: Alex Stamos on how AI is upending cybersecurity. Here we go. I feel like you and I talked a lot about how all that was working, about election security, all those sorts of things. We’re in a new era of big problems on the internet, particularly around cyber defense, cybersecurity. You’ve been thinking about this stuff a lot. What’s been less discussed is a huge number of companies have been breached. You have a series of AI-related companies, the neoclouds that have been breached in succession. item.title: Fireworks says you’re wasting money on AI unless you’re using all the models
item.description: Fireworks AI is fine with helping companies run AI models in their own datacenters, though VP Rob Ferguson argues against doing so. Ferguson told The Register in an interview that while Fireworks AI, a managed inference provider, supports on-prem AI, "we're trying to push people more and more away from it because frankly, it's just the economics." The GPU hardware is just so expensive that if you can't keep it fully utilized, it's a waste of money, he contends. Ten thousand GPUs, he said, represent a billion dollars of capital. "You don't want those things to be sitting idle," he said. For companies with particularly sensitive workloads, Ferguson said, Fireworks is happy to work something out – it offers a service called Sovereign for just that purpose and it has partners like Microsoft that can help. But most inference work probably doesn't need that level of protection, he said. "The state of the art for everyone is to have a portfolio of models," he explained. "In fact, I think most people don't know that the best model in the world's not Astra. The best model in the world's not Fable. The best model is literally a portfolio and we can prove it. You are always better routing between a few models than to do one singular model." That's what Fireworks does through Nexus and its API, alongside competitors like Together AI, Baseten, and DeepInfra. As a managed inference platform, Fireworks AI routes inference tasks to whichever model, frontier model subscription, or API is best suited to handle them. But the company is not just doing naive routing like an AI gateway. It's evaluating tasks as they come in and directing them to the optimal model. "We build custom routers," Ferguson explained. "Our auto model is continuously updating so that we actually go through and we grade the difficulty of the task and we see if there're affinities that the models have, like Kimi is slightly better at JavaScript than Python, things like this." The company's competitive edge, he contends, is its crack engineering team, which follows from its founders' work on PyTorch, a widely used open source machine learning library. "We're performance experts both on the training and inference side," he explained. "People I think don't understand how important, for example, numerics is. So when you use a model, it's always called a mixture of experts – an expert is a different machine. "And so you have all these different machines. It actually matters when you're training that you go back to precisely the right machine, because if you don't, the other machine will still answer the question, but it'll answer in a slightly different way. So we have to know how to build the topology to write back the data to the right space. We have to understand floating point precision [to handle very small values]. We have to be able to do all this where we're routing through a complex fabric through potentially more than one provider depending on what everything is. And so we're really systems

item.title: Star Wars is experiencing a golden age of video games
item.description: After a tumultuous start to EA's rebooted Star Wars Battlefront series, in 2021 Lucasfilm and Disney decided to open up the development of new Star Wars games by bringing in different publishers and studios under the Lucasfilm Games banner. Now, over five years on, we can confidently say we're entering a new golden era of amazing Star Wars games . With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences. It's become clear that future Star Wars games needn't be expensive endeavors full of familiar faces or concepts. Star Wars Zero Company and Galactic Racer 's restrained scope and confidence have been infectious, and, as it turns out, they're already recognized by all the parties involved as double-A success stories . Now this is podracing! (Image credit: Secret Mode) A Burnout-inspired Star Wars racer (created by a bunch of ex-Burnout devs) is a fantastic pitch if you know your video games, but looking at EA's recent and current direction, it's easy to see why it didn't happen under their reign. The original Burnout studio, Criterion, would have been an excellent candidate, but instead they were sent to work in the Battlefield mines. Still, someone was interested in the idea, and the end result is glorious. Fast and furious, Star Wars: Galactic Racer ignores recent racing game trends and bets big on arcade-y vibes, uncomplicated controls, and a high skill ceiling that challenges you with extremely high speeds, tight turns, and unexpected interruptions as other drivers try to ruin your day. The not-so-secret sauce, however, was its runs-based structure, which injects the flexibility and replay value of roguelite games into the more traditional arcade racing structure that older gamers are familiar with. (Image credit: EA) Fully confident in its central gameplay idea and devoid of modern live-service baggage, Fuse Games' debut title makes the most of the Star Wars setting within the restrictions of simply making a fun and engaging Star Wars racer. It's almost the same approach we felt in Zero Company, a turn-based tactical strategy-RPG that comes from the minds of another team of ex-triple-A developers. "Star Wars but XCOM" should've happened earlier, but we're glad it did this year, and, unsurprisingly, it's a banger. The correct read of their success should be obvious (and so far, it appears the powers that be are seeing it): Let seasoned and fresh developers cook games they're excited about. Big, medium, or small, players will react positively to experiences that really feel genuine and aren't brought down by tacked-on systems or monetization. item.title: The Bantu expansion changed Africa. Scientists are still tracing how.
item.description: It’s not easy to extract iron from its ore. But the peoples of the ancient city of Great Zimbabwe—the capital of a thriving kingdom in southern Africa between 1000 to 1700 AD—were masters. At sites near the city’s stone ruins, clusters of iron-smelting furnaces survive today as mounds of rubble. At Mashava, a village 25 miles northwest, fragments bear fingermarks of those who long ago smoothed the structures’ clay interiors. Some of the furnaces were nearly an adult’s arm span in width, with walls thick and strong to contain the heat of more than 2,100° Fahrenheit needed to smelt iron. Unlike other furnaces that required workers to force air into them with bellows, these were designed to suck air in, then out through a chimney, no human labor required. This would have made it significantly easier to produce the iron, which was fashioned into hoes, axes, and arrowheads. Read full article Comments

item.title: 'I think we will prevail': NASA chief Jared Isaacman on Artemis, China and the new moon race (exclusive)
item.description: null NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is serious about launching "big rockets" to the moon every single year for the agency's Artemis program. And the new space race with China is fueling that ambition. "I feel good. I feel like we are certainly on a more achievable path to the lunar surface today than where we were before," Isaacman told Space.com. We recently sat down with the NASA chief to discuss the state of the Artemis program , and, off the bat, he made it clear that he's confident in the U.S. space program following the success of April's Artemis II mission around the moon. In fact, just prior to our conversation, it was announced that Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman will become the new deputy director of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. But the road from Artemis II's success to crewed lunar landings and, later, a permanent moon base will take a lot of launches of NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) megarocket, Isaacman stressed. "You know, a lot of people, especially in the space community, start getting [into] if the landers are there or not. I don't really care about that right now. What I care about is that we are launching big rockets no less than once a year," he said. "I think that's imperative for NASA to be doing these deep-space human spaceflight missions right now," Isaacman added. "So, we had a great mission in April of '26. We will launch again in '27." That coming launch will be for Artemis III, a crewed mission to low Earth orbit that will test docking procedures between NASA's Orion capsule and one or both of the Artemis program's private lunar landers — SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon. "We need to continue to exercise those muscles," he said, referring to SLS liftoffs. "And, honestly, once a year isn't great, either. I mean, I don't think we're going to get back to the early [space] shuttle days, you know, four missions a year. I don't think we're going to get back to where we were with Apollo, but once a year is the minimum … I would testify that to Congress in this role years down the road. "If NASA is going to be doing deep-space missions, complicated missions, [we should] launch at least once a year and get as much out of it as you can for taking the risk and spending the taxpayer dollars and building towards something greater," Isaacman added. "That's what we're doing with Artemis III, and that's what's going to better prepare us for Artemis IV." A new space race So, how is NASA coping with the challenges that face them as they approach Artemis III ahead of a crewed lunar landing on Artemis IV, which is targeted for 2028? While NASA can learn some lessons from past moon missions with Apollo, today it's primarily relying on the extensive experience and talent within the agency, according to Isaacman. "Artemis II is very different from Apollo 8, and Artemis III will be very different from Apollo 9," he said. "Our approach is not exactly the same as it was … But what is the same right now? item.title: NHS breach helpline left staff carrying a 'significant emotional burden'
item.description: NHS staff drafted into a helpline after colleagues' health data was exposed online faced distressed callers, safeguarding concerns, and a "serious emotional impact," a review has found. The report [PDF] comes almost exactly a year after the Royal Cornwall Hospitals NHS Trust disclosed a data breach affecting 8,003 people, including current and former trust staff and non-trust workers. A member of the public discovered the exposure in November 2025. An Excel workbook published in response to a Freedom of Information request in February 2023 retained underlying sickness absence records that users could reveal through its pivot tables. Staff assigned to the helpline described difficult calls involving shouting, anger, and distress. Particularly difficult calls involved people distressed by the sensitivity of the disclosures or potentially in danger from domestic abuse. Call handlers said they had to make safeguarding assessments without training or an established process. "Such occurrences of anger or distress were not infrequent, and this reflected the heightened emotions and distress experienced by callers to varying degrees due to the breach," the review noted. "This placed significant emotional burden on individuals working in the contact center, who were not prepared or provided support on how to deal with those." Members of the trust's clinical governance team were told just a day beforehand that they would staff the helpline. Despite their experience dealing with patient trauma, they received little preparation for the calls that followed. "The staff working in the call centers had a short training session and then the calls started coming in within minutes of the team being set up," the review noted. "Some staff had not finished reading the pre-prepared script which had arrived only 30 minutes before the center went live." Most call handlers only learned that their own data had been exposed while already working on the helpline, sometimes minutes before supporting others affected. Call handlers also said they had little choice about taking on the work and were expected to maintain their usual duties alongside it. The review stated that some staff members gave up weekends and worked long past their scheduled hours to meet the demands of both roles. "It's typical NHS, it runs on goodwill," one staffer told the team that compiled the report. The call center was only supposed to run for two weeks in December 2025, but due to the volume of calls, it was eventually stood down after 11 weeks, in February 2026. According to officials speaking at a trust board meeting on Thursday, the review and its findings have since been circulated among staff, and published online. How the spreadsheet slipped through Responding to a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request thought to be from a journalist researching a story about stress in the NHS, the Royal Cornwall Hospitals NHS Trust uploaded a spreadsheet to its public FOI Disclosure log in February 2023. item.title: The datacentre arms race hits pause in south-east Asia
item.description: Power and water constraints are pressuring what seemed like a juggernaut of growth for the region just months ago In early 2026, Thailand’s datacentre industry was on a roll. The country’s board of investment had recently announced approval of datacentre projects from Tiktok, a UAE-based Skyline datacentre and Singapore’s Bridge datacentres, totalling a planned investment of $27bn. As the year has passed, however, what once seemed like a new industrial juggernaut has ground to a halt. Thailand paused construction on 49 projects and approval decisions on 117 more in September 2026, amidst growing concern about the lack of sufficient details for regulation and monitoring. It is not alone in reconsidering datacentre projects. In neighbouring Indonesia, the governor of the country’s most populous province of West Java halted construction on a datacentre due to lack of permits and an incomplete environmental assessment process. Despite the many faces of 2026, the ups and downs, Nigerians and Africans showed up on big stages to express their creativity and talent. It was this year that Nora Awolowo and Damilola Osikoya broke the Guinness World Record for the largest attendance at a film screening with the screening of Black Market: The Movie . It was in 2026 that Ogaga Ifowodo won the $100,000 Nigeria Prize for Literature. It was in 2026 that Kayinsola Ajayi broke Nigeria’s 100m record. And many many more. At BellaNaija, it was an even greater and more remarkable year. We celebrated our 20th anniversary with a Grand Red Carpet Experience. It was a beautiful evening that marked and solidified BellaNaija’s contribution as one of the culture shapers in Africa. Beyond the red carpet experience, it was the year of stories. We told stories of Africans and Nigerians achieving incredible feats at home and abroad. We told stories of educational success, stories of love, of Africans across the world. We did only what we are meant to do, and what we know best to do. So we want to hear from you too. We want to know how 2026 has been for you. Did you start a new job? Did you find love? Did you start a new hobby or routine? Did you buy something you’ve always wanted? How were your finances? What experience from the year stood out for you? What did you manage to achieve? What did you fail to achieve? Share any experiences that brought you down, but also taught you how to pick yourself back up. We want to hear about it all. We want you to write all about it. Reflect on moments when you wished you had made different choices. Share instances where you chose to trust your intuition. Tell us about the beautiful experiences you had this year. We invite you to share your victories and setbacks, as well as your joys and sorrows, with us. You have a lot to get a lot off your chest, and we are also ready to read, so share with us. Guidelines : Send your #BN2026Epilogues stories to features@bellanaija.com Include 2026 Epilogues in the subject of your email. Stories can be between 400 and 1,500 words. item.title: Windows takes a break at UK motorway services
item.description: A roadside display at Cherwell Valley services has stopped dispensing information and started asking for help. The eagle-eyed Register reader who spotted the stricken screen told us: "UK motorway signs often tell us that tiredness can kill, urging us to take a break. This poor thing at Cherwell Valley services took the advice to heart." The display at the Moto services appears to have run into trouble during a restart. Windows offers another attempt or access to repair tools, although the latter options are hidden – perhaps somewhere on the top floor of the neighboring Travelodge. Getting things moving again will probably require access to the computer behind the screen. The Automatic Repair screen is all too familiar to Windows users. Not to be confused with the classic blue screen of death, it might indicate a misbehaving driver during a reboot, an update that did something unexpected, or some sort of hardware failure. Hopefully it isn't the latter – with memory and storage prices the way they are at the moment, a motorway services sandwich or gallon of fuel will seem a positive bargain by comparison. Our reader is right: taking a break is sensible advice. Getting Windows to end one can be another matter. ®

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 7 – De Gerlache-Kocher Massif
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 7 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. De Gerlache-Kocher Massif Explanation: De Gerlache-Kocher massif looms on the visible horizon in this close-up of the edge of the Moon. The mountainous formation rises about 4 kilometers above its surroundings and is located very close to the lunar south pole. Boasting permanently shadowed crater floors that likely contain deposits of water ice and peaks that receive almost continuous sunlight for solar power generation, the south polar region is consider a prime location for the first human settlement on the Moon. In fact , De Gerlache-Kocher massif itself has been considered as a potential landing site for future crewed Artemis missions to the Moon . The remarkable telescopic image of the massif at the lunar limb was captured on October 31. Then, a favorable libration angle or lunar wobble enhanced this oblique view across the Moon’s south pole. item.title: Freezer meltdowns and airline hoaxes are a taste of things to come. Hoping for the best is no longer an option | Elisabeth Braw
item.description: Acts of greyzone aggression aim to spread panic. Europe has to show the saboteurs that we are resilient It was as though a ghostly hand had switched the settings on supermarket freezers across Europe from “freeze” to “defrost”. From Finland to Ireland, they suddenly began heating up , many reaching 50C and food worth millions of euros had to be thrown away. But no actual hand was needed to cause the meltdown. This was a cyber-attack, or rather a chain of attacks. Like pretty much everything else in 2026, supermarket freezers are digitally enabled. That makes them smarter and more efficient, but like everything else that is connected to the internet, it also makes them more vulnerable. Russian hacktivists claimed they were behind some of the supermarket sabotage, but no one knows for sure. It could also be Iran, Iranian proxies, North Korea – or unaffiliated bedroom hackers. When Transport for London suffered a devastating hack two years ago, the culprits turned out to be two British teenagers . Governments regularly warn retailers and other companies about cyber-attacks and even provide cyber-defence training to businesses . The lessons of costly ransomware and cyber-attacks also mean many big organisations and retailers have become much better at keeping their payments and logistics systems safe. Elisabeth Braw is a Swedish security expert and the author of The Undersea War : The International Battle for Supremacy at the Bottom of the World Continue reading...

item.title: SpaceX launches mystery mission for US Space Force in gorgeous sunset liftoff from California (video, photos)
item.description: null SpaceX just launched a classified mission for the U.S. military. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base this evening (Nov. 6) at 7:48 p.m. EST (4:48 p.m. local California time; 0048 GMT on Nov. 7), rising into the sky as the sun sank toward the Pacific. The launch kicked off the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force , which we know little about. Neither SpaceX nor the Space Force told us much about USSF-432 beforehand, and we learned tonight; SpaceX cut its webcast off about 10 minutes into the flight, shortly after the Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth for a landing. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base on Nov. 6, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) That touchdown occurred aboard the SpaceX droneship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed downrange in the Pacific Ocean. It wrapped up the eighth flight for this particular booster, which is designated 1095. The Falcon 9's upper stage, meanwhile, continued carrying its mystery payload skyward. It could be headed to low Earth orbit , outside observers speculate. "It is possibly a batch of classified LEO satellites for the USSF's Space Based Sensing and Targeting (SBST) portfolio based on SpaceX's Starshield satellite bus, based on locations of rocket stage drop zones being exact fits with previous Starlink Group 15 launches," NextSpaceflight.com wrote in a mission description . Starlink is SpaceX's LEO broadband megaconstellation, which consists of more than 11,000 active satellites. Starshield is a similar system designed to provide services to the U.S. military and its allies. Starshield satellites are believed to be based heavily on the Starlink spacecraft bus. The Falcon 9's first stage after its landing on Nov. 6, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) Previous Booster 1095 missions GPS-III 8 | 6 Starlink missions USSF-432 was the 119th Falcon 9 launch of 2026, and the 14th national-security flight of the rocket so far this year. The vast majority of Falcon 9 missions in 2026 — more than 70% — have been devoted to building out the Starlink megaconstellation. SpaceX has also launched six other missions this year. Three were operational flights of the company's Falcon Heavy rocket, while the other three were test missions of its next-gen Starship vehicle. SpaceX plans to retire both the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy shortly after the fully reusable Starship, the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built, is up and running.

item.title: Doctors pull knife from man's eye that went through his brain—and he's fine now
item.description: A man in his 20s showed up to a UK hospital with the hilt of a knife sticking out of his face. The 15 mm-wide blade hidden within went completely through his right eye and through his brain, with the tip of the blade hitting the top of his skull. Despite the ghastly injury, the man was alive and conscious when he arrived. He could still talk and move all four limbs. His doctors described him as being in a state of agitation. On the Glasgow Coma Scale, he scored a 12 (E3 V4 M5) , indicating a "moderate" brain injury, just one point above "mild." He could open his left eye when told, but otherwise kept it closed (E3 score); he could talk and answer questions, but was confused (V4); and he intentionally moved away when pressure was applied to his body (M5). In a report published Friday in BMJ Case Report, his doctors said they were concerned that in his confused, agitated state he may try to pull the knife out on his own. So, they swiftly sedated and intubated him. They put him on prophylactic treatments for bacterial infections, including tetanus. Then they used images to see what was going on in his head. item.title: Ships loiter near subsea cables amid Iran's warnings to Trump
item.description: Several tanker ships linked to Iran have been loitering over subsea Internet cables in the Gulf of Oman near the Strait of Hormuz—a possible indication that the Iranian government is preparing to attack such undersea infrastructure in response to any renewed US and Israeli strikes. The movements of three sanctioned tankers and an Iranian fishing boat have been tracked near major undersea cables by the maritime intelligence firm Windward in October, according to the Financial Times . Six active cables currently cross through the contested Strait of Hormuz, linking the Middle East to Europe, Africa and Asia, with two more cables having segments under construction in the region. Four countries, including Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar, depend entirely upon such subsea telecommunications connections running through the Strait of Hormuz chokepoint to link with the outside world. But other countries also depend heavily on the region's undersea cable network—one third of India’s westbound Internet traffic goes through the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
item.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: AST SpaceMobile announces new 'Blacklift' rocket, targets 2028 launch debut
item.description: null Another new private rocket is in the works. AST SpaceMobile announced today (Nov. 6) that it's building a reusable rocket called Blacklift to launch its broadband satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO), with first flight targeted in 2028. The news comes just 10 days after Cowboy Space unveiled Big Iron , a rocket designed to launch its constellation of 20,000 AI data centers . Cowboy Space is also targeting 2028 for its first liftoff. "The Blacklift rocket is the springboard to significantly expand our total addressable market, providing AST SpaceMobile with regular unconstrained access to orbit and providing for most favorable owners’ economics in the industry," Abel Avellan, the company's founder, chairman and CEO, said in a statement today . "This will accelerate our mission to build a new layer of global connectivity, extending connectivity beyond terrestrial networks and helping to bring AI-enabled services wherever people live, work and travel," Avellan added. Texas-based AST SpaceMobile is building a LEO constellation composed of its BlueBird satellites , which beam internet service directly to cell phones. The company has launched 13 BlueBirds to date, including eight "Block 2" variants. The antennas on each of these next-gen spacecraft cover a whopping 2,400 square feet (223 square m) — the largest ever deployed in LEO by a commercial satellite. BlueBirds have flown atop three different rockets to date — SpaceX's Falcon 9 , Blue Origin's New Glenn and India's Launch Vehicle Mark-3. But AST SpaceMobile wants to get more vertically integrated, which explains the push to develop Blacklift. The company won't be starting from scratch. It has signed a deal with another Texas-based outfit, Firefly Aerospace , to provide the engines (and associated engineering services) for the first three Blacklift launches. After that, AST SpaceMobile will build the engines itself, under a licensing agreement with Firefly. Those engines are Miranda, which will power Blacklift's booster, and Vira, which will power the upper stage. Neither engine has flight experience. (Firefly's currently operational rocket, Alpha, uses Reavers in its booster and Lightnings in its upper stage.) But Miranda has been tested extensively on the ground, firing for more than 4,200 seconds over the course of 175 hot fires, according to AST SpaceMobile. "The Miranda engine will allow us to leapfrog the traditional five-to-10-year development cycle as we build Blacklift," AST SpaceMobile President Scott Wisniewski said in the same statement. The "supply and services" agreement for the first three launches is worth $500 million. The licensing agreement cost AST SpaceMobile about $800 million, with half of that paid in cash and half in stock, according to the statement. Blacklift will be able to haul 20 tons to LEO. Each launch will therefore be able to loft up to five BlueBird satellites, according to today's announcement. (For perspective: The Falcon 9's LEO lift capacity is about 25
